9efe0f33.en: Faction and server choice is permanent, faction-locked, and mostly cosmetic, so pick where your friends are.

8322a8af.en: Faction and server choice is a single, largely permanent decision. Elyos and Asmodians sit on faction-exclusive servers, and you generally only meet the other faction in instanced content, Abyss battles, or specific events.

ca1b0a15.en: There is currently no stated way to switch factions later. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧

9690e96e.en: Both factions share the same 8 classes and the same faction-war endgame; there is no evidence of a power difference between them, so the choice is cosmetic and social rather than a power tier. Elyos start in Poeta (western, light-aligned, capital Sanctum); Asmodians occupy the eastern/dark-aligned side.

523aff75.en: Beginner tip: because Legions (guilds) are faction-locked, picking the same faction and server as friends matters far more here than in games where players can freely mix.

a3a2c23d.en: Classes (8 total), trinity-organized: Tank, Templar; Melee DPS, Gladiator and Assassin; Ranged physical DPS, Ranger; Magic DPS, Sorcerer and Spiritmaster; Healer, Cleric; Hybrid support, Chanter. single source, lower-trust ⟦1⟧

d3c25ac9.en: Past 84 dungeon clears a week, your whole account's tradeable Kinah and gear drops get cut hard.

8e6f8422.en: Once an account registers 84 combined dungeon clears within a single weekly lockout period, tradeable Kinah and gear drops are reduced (one source says by 90%) for the rest of that week, across all characters on the account, not just the one that hit the threshold.
8e6f8422.ctx: start / Alt characters and the 84-run rule

9eabc059.en: The restriction is account-wide by design, to stop players from running many alts to funnel loot onto one main character. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧
9eabc059.ctx: start / Alt characters and the 84-run rule

9ffbc03e.en: Kinah splits into Bound Kinah (non-tradeable, usable for NPC costs) and Tradeable Kinah (broker-eligible); only tradeable drops are affected by the 84-run penalty, so bound-currency income for alts is unaffected. single source ⟦1⟧
9ffbc03e.ctx: start / Alt characters and the 84-run rule

49d6ba0d.ctx: start / Alt characters and the 84-run rule

d9152ebe.en: Community guides suggest running up to roughly 84 dungeon clears per account per week for full Kinah efficiency; beyond that, efficiency drops sharply, with a second breakpoint around 126 runs cited for players chasing materials rather than Kinah. single source, unverified ⟦1⟧
d9152ebe.ctx: start / Alt characters and the 84-run rule

e8907ac9.en: Beginner tip: focus one main character until it reaches the power threshold where clears become fast, before investing in alts. Per-character systems (Daeva Pass, Stigma, gear) do not share progress. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

b07f12a8.en: Tension worth noting: the Daeva Pass is sold per character, which incentivizes alts, while the 84-run system discourages heavy alt-running for Kinah. Rolling one or two alts for Daeva Pass or side content appears fine; running dozens purely to farm dungeon loot is what the 84-run system targets.

9bb1a889.en: Beginner tip: "Gear Score" is community slang. The game itself uses item level (gear-only, gates dungeon entry) and combat power (a broader number including Daevanion talents, Pantheon unlocks, Arcana cards, and skill levels). Do not confuse the two: a dungeon's stated item-level minimum can still be a hard failure if your combat power isn't there yet. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

acae3825.en: AION 2 layers well over a dozen progression systems on top of your base class. The cards below are listed roughly in unlock order, from the skills you touch at level 1 through to endgame Combat Power grinding, so you can read top to bottom as a rough roadmap.

fc95ada8.en: Global launches October 5, 2026, and most numbers here come from the KR/TW live client, so treat exact thresholds as subject to change.

4ddadcc4.en: Mastery Skills level automatically; spend Skill Points on your core 3-4 rotation abilities.

92c27df5.en: Mastery Skills are your core class abilities. They are learned automatically as you hit level requirements. ⟦1⟧

b08c724f.en: Every level-up grants Skill Points, which you spend to raise a Mastery Skill up to a base cap of 10. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

4e0b6c2f.en: Skill Points can be refunded for a small Kinah fee, so early experimentation is safe ⟦1⟧.

208f0edf.en: Daevanion board and gear effects can push a skill's effective level to 12 or 16, past the base cap of 10 ⟦1⟧.

4bbb6d86.en: At skill breakpoints of level 8, 12, and 16, you can pick up to 3 additional chosen effects, called Specialization ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

5f30f442.en: Extra Skill Points come from Empyrean Traces, world collectibles turned in at a Monolith for Wisdom Stones, an item that grants Skill Points on use. ⟦1⟧

da175324.en: A separate guide calls the same collectible simply "Feathers" turned in at city Monoliths. ⟦1⟧

20e447af.en: Korean class-board guides from 2026 routinely talk about pushing core skills to skill level 20, and some to 25, above the 8/12/16 breakpoints described here. That ceiling is reached with Daevanion, Stigma and Arcana bonuses stacked on the base cap, and no single source states the current maximum, so treat the top breakpoint as KR-era and unverified for global kr-era ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧. The per-class Leveling build cards give the skill-level targets those guides use.

b70957b0.en: Naming is inconsistent between sources: "Empyrean Traces"/"Wisdom Stones" versus "Feathers" are likely different translations of the same KR-era item, so treat the exact item names as contested.

c00f091b.en: Beginner priority: put points into your main damage chain, a self-heal or HP recovery skill, and anything usable while moving, then push your rotation's core 3-4 abilities past the 8/12/16 breakpoints ⟦1⟧.

81b55366.en: Common mistake: spreading Skill Points thin across many skills instead of concentrating on your rotation's core abilities.

dd8b94b0.en: Stigmas add build-defining abilities; sources disagree on exactly which levels unlock which slots.

e8253310.en: Stigmas are equippable skill-enhancement stones that add build-defining abilities on top of your class kit. ⟦1⟧ They consume a separate currency, Stigma Shards, rather than normal Skill Points. ⟦2⟧

fa988dae.en: One detailed source says the first Stigma slot unlocks at level 23, with two more normal slots at 30 and 40, two Greater Stigma slots at 45 and 50, and a Major Stigma slot at 55 ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

62a086e4.en: A second source instead says Stigmas unlock at level 23 with up to four equipped at once, which conflicts with the 23/30/40/45/50/55 breakdown above ⟦1⟧.

4def45df.en: Level 45 is confirmed to unlock two Greater Stigma slots via a group quest, "The Shattered Stigma" for Elyos or "The Shulak's Stigma" for Asmodians ⟦1⟧.

b256f992.en: KR-era content raised the Stigma level cap from 20 to 25, requiring a higher-tier Shard above level 20; this is explicitly flagged as KR-only and unconfirmed for global ⟦1⟧ kr-era.

11ae43d4.en: Beginner priority: pick a single PvE rotation and fund the Stigmas that fill actual gaps in it, upgrading your most-used Stigma first rather than spreading Shards across every Stigma you own ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

c3ef9411.en: Common mistake: building a PvP Stigma set before you have a stable PvE rotation, which wastes scarce Shards.

f7f5b141.en: Six Daevanion Boards unlock through level 45 and add permanent combat stats separate from gear.

27427cfb.en: A permanent node-board progression system, separate from gear, that raises combat stats and effective skill levels. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

f6390ca6.en: The first board unlocks at level 12; one detailed source states there are 6 total boards unlocking progressively, with the last two arriving at level 45 ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

d8623a8d.en: Daevanion Points unlock nodes; Points and Daevanion Crystals both come from regional quests, Sealed Dungeons, Strongholds, achievements, and exploration ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧.

74742ebe.en: The KR client can reset a whole board or individual nodes, with a single-node reset costing 500 Kinah in Korea. ⟦1⟧ kr-era, self-flagged as provisional

ca6acf5f.en: A node cannot be removed while another already-acquired node depends on it. The source explicitly flags that Global's final reset costs, caps, and terminology may differ from what shipped in Korea.

f6446689.en: Separately, Korean community discussion claims a recent patch "significantly reduced" reset costs for both skills and Daevanion nodes, without giving a before/after number, consistent with but not independent confirmation of the 500 Kinah figure. single source, vague ⟦1⟧

18ca7848.en: Gold/orange nodes are passive stat boosts, blue nodes amplify active skills, and green nodes optimize existing passives like resource regen, per one summary. ⟦1⟧

ded2d849.en: A second source describes essentially the same split as "skill nodes" and "stat nodes" without the color breakdown, a likely simplification rather than a contradiction.

d94bcf5a.en: The board is cited as a source of 500+ "passive" Combat Power that does not require gear swapping, earned by clearing hidden question-mark dungeons, Sealed Dungeons, and Strongholds ⟦1⟧.

dd65c536.en: Beginner priority: trace the cheapest path to skill/stat nodes that support one specific loadout, comparing full routes by total point cost rather than grabbing every nearby node purely for Combat Power ⟦1⟧.

f346a8d2.en: Common mistake: neglecting the board while rushing the main story; it's a significant permanent power source that's easy to overlook ⟦1⟧.

2bed0070.en: No official AION 2 global skill or stigma-name glossary has been published pre-launch. The official global-facing material found only confirms the roster of 8 launch classes plus an unconfirmed 9th (Brawler, seen in KR/TW) and a Launch Scale Test running September 17-18, 2026 single source, marketing-aggregator, not the official site itself ⟦1⟧. All node and skill names used on this page are fan translations from community guides, not official localizations, unless otherwise noted.

48a6bfcb.en: Arcana cards add item level, stats, and set bonuses; fill every slot rather than chasing perfect rarity.

f24b3ca5.en: A card-based system that adds Item Level, combat stats, set bonuses, and effective skill levels all at once. ⟦1⟧

aefdab56.en: Original slot types are Chalice, Parchment, Compass, Bell, and Mirror; later content reportedly added Scales, Key, Hourglass, Dice, and Lantern, for up to nine slots total. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

6abead9d.en: More precisely, the card-slot rollout came in generations: the original five (Chalice, Parchment, Compass, Bell, Mirror), Scales added in "Season 2," and Key, Hourglass, Dice, and Lantern added in "Chapter 1." single source ⟦1⟧

da0dab70.en: Rarity tiers cited are Common (about +20 item level), Rare (+40), Epic (+60), and Unique (+80), affecting a card's overall item-level contribution. ⟦1⟧

48cf9aae.en: A separate source uses "green 40, blue 60, unique 80" for the same slots, suggesting a rarity-name translation mismatch between sources.

798cc95d.en: Cards come primarily from Transcendence dungeons tied to specific slots, sets, and crystal families, ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ plus crafting/synthesis, extraction from unwanted cards, and events.

56a8bf69.en: The guidance is to pick a dungeon for its Arcana output rather than for its difficulty stage alone. single source ⟦1⟧

b9fafa9d.en: Cards gain experience from Training Arcana consumables (Lesser 200 EXP, Intermediate 600, Superior 1,500, Ultimate 3,000) or by feeding in other cards. ⟦1⟧

d2b063ce.en: Skill-level bonuses stack with Stigma and Daevanion bonuses toward the same 16-20 breakpoints. Equipping five different cards is separately said to "significantly increase" skill levels and Combat Power. ⟦1⟧

e33aac43.en: Targeted cards can also be crafted directly using tiered crystals, Mysterious, Harmonious, Noble, or Splendent Noble depending on card generation, plus Kinah single source, detailed ⟦1⟧.

36550ed0.en: Beginner priority: fill every slot with something usable rather than waiting for a perfect Unique card, protect skill breakpoints and set bonuses over raw item level, save Training Arcana for cards you plan to keep, and farm the Transcendence dungeon that matches the slot or crystal family you actually need ⟦1⟧.

a60ca9d9.en: Common mistake: leaving slots empty, farming the wrong dungeon for prestige, over-enhancing filler cards, or destroying a card before confirming its replacement is actually equipped ⟦1⟧.

14af22cb.en: Flag: this progression system, dungeon-gated drops, tiered EXP materials, and crystal crafting, is exactly the kind of thing that could change materially for global launch, so treat every figure above as KR-era kr-era. No official global skill-name glossary exists either, so card-to-skill assignments quoted elsewhere on this page are fan translations, not confirmed localizations ⟦1⟧.

a3d1e939.en: Gear from questing, loot, and the Broker

58a42c2d.en: Gear grade names vary by source; enhance evenly across slots before pushing any one piece high.

92c5f297.en: NCSoft's own patch notes reportedly confirm at least Heroic and Unique grades, with Unique higher. ⟦1⟧

784fea2c.en: Community sources also describe a wider tier list, Rare from standard dungeons, Unique from Hard Mode, Legendary from Nightmare/Abyss content, alongside a separate Green/Blue/Purple/Gold color scheme used for Pantheon items, so grade naming is not fully consistent across sources.

4e721ad9.en: Enhance Stones raise a gear piece's level; enchanting adds PvE Attack/Defense on PvE gear or PvP Attack/Defense on PvP gear depending on item type ⟦1⟧.

54109379.en: Failing an enchant does not destroy the item, and extracting a previously-enhanced item refunds 100% of the Enhance Stones spent into it ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

c52d73f5.en: Suggested safe breakpoints to stop and bank Kinah: +3-5, +8 ("damage smoothing", especially for weapons), +10 (feels properly progressed), +12 (controlled risk on good gear), and +15 (only for long-term keeper gear) ⟦1⟧.

03677aad.en: Mana Stones socket into gear for stats like Crit Rate or Speed, helping gear "scale into late-game without major farming" alongside Soul Codexes. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

5eb4c0bf.en: A separate single source describes an "engraving" mechanic where one attempt rerolls every socket, uncorroborated elsewhere.

4dcf054b.en: Gear comes from questing, world/dungeon loot, and the player marketplace or Broker ⟦1⟧.

15520092.en: Beginner priority: enhance your weapon first since it gives the single biggest damage boost, then survivability armor, then remaining armor, then accessories last ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

a7054d34.en: Avoid: pushing one piece to a high, risky enhancement level before your other slots have reached a low safe tier.

136d969e.en: Mana Stones and Theostones are socketed gems and weapon procs, slot them in as they drop.

a474dd1f.en: Mana Stones are AION 2's socketed stat gems, found via dungeons, rewards, or crafting. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ Theostones are the weapon proc-stone equivalent of classic AION's Godstones.

3d1f2f31.en: Theostones socket into a weapon's dedicated slot and grant a chance-on-hit proc effect such as damage or a debuff; one effect per weapon, and identical Theostones do not stack ⟦1⟧.

73626969.en: A community database lists 153 known Theostones, corroborated across three independent sources ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

3c79b4be.en: Beginner priority: treat Mana Stones and Theostones as gradual scaling tools you slot in as they drop, rather than something to farm dedicated runs for early on.

4c96eeb4.en: Grows once bound, per one source

8d79be23.en: One uncorroborated source says bound gear gains a growing secondary stat; bind and use gear normally.

7789ecc4.en: Described by one fan-run compiled wiki as a secondary stat block on gear that "only grows once you bind it." ⟦1⟧ This is likely analogous to classic AION's soul-binding-on-equip mechanic but with an added stat-growth twist here.

ab9c4854.en: Not corroborated by any other source found; treat the whole mechanic as single-source and uncertain until confirmed elsewhere.

0dc2f780.en: Beginner priority: bind and use gear normally, since even the single source describing this doesn't suggest a reason to delay binding.

4b7c4b86.en: Pantheon is an unconfirmed passive-stat system, slot pieces in opportunistically, don't farm it dedicated.

d4b91e98.en: An "often overlooked" permanent passive-stat system built from Statues, Colossi, and "Artwork"/frameworks; placing a Colossus into a Pantheon slot grants points toward one of several "deity domains," each capping at 200 points before converting into flat combat stats. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

b7c0bc5c.en: Item rarity (Green to Blue to Purple to Gold) determines each piece's bonus strength, with Green giving 40 stat points and Blue 60 in one cited example.

568ac9b5.en: Named domains include Wisdom (strike chance/final damage), Freedom (accuracy/evasion), and Death (critical hit chance) ⟦1⟧.

a62c3667.en: This system rests on a small cluster of corroborating community sources, mostly one aggregator plus a boosting site, with no wiki or database confirmation found. Treat the whole Pantheon system as not independently confirmed, though the name itself appears consistently.

89b64e35.en: Beginner priority: treat Pantheon pieces as passive value you slot in opportunistically rather than a system worth dedicated farming until it's better confirmed for global.

50be2f65.en: Achievements and titles come from normal play, don't farm them as a separate track.

12934824.en: Achievements grant Achievement Points and rewards, and completing them ties into Daevanion Point/Crystal income. ⟦1⟧

c7bcd790.en: One database lists 1,307 achievements, while a differing count elsewhere cites 4,225 named achievements across grades, categories, and factions, of which 2,685 grant rewards; likely different snapshots or counting methods ⟦1⟧.

ed0811ff.en: Titles: one source counts 1,472 total titles with 844 granting stat bonuses, earned via PvP rank, Arena tiers, boss kills, monster-hunting milestones, server-first accomplishments, and mini-game/event wins. ⟦1⟧

933f620d.en: Stat titles grant things like PvP Attack, PvP Accuracy, HP, Defense, Combat/Move Speed, or Critical Hit; some titles are purely cosmetic.

87db28a4.en: A separate source states you can have 3 active title effects at once across Offensive/Defensive/Other categories, unlocking around level 30; this slot count and level could not be cross-confirmed, treat as single-source.

6144508d.en: An Appearance Collection (wardrobe) exists; collecting roughly 700 appearances grants combat speed and cooldown reduction as a milestone bonus. ⟦1⟧

b1ab7c07.en: Cash-shop cosmetics do not count toward this bonus, though they do count for achievements.

1e20a6a5.en: Beginner priority: don't farm titles or achievements as a separate track early; treat them as a byproduct of normal questing and dungeon clears, and periodically check the achievement panel for cheap stat titles you already qualify for.

ec174659.en: Pets double as mounts, farm 10 "souls" of a monster to unlock each one.

2d380d4e.en: Pets and mounts are the same system in AION 2: any pet you own can also be ridden as a mount. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ Over 200 pets are collectible. ⟦3⟧

dd0f2449.en: The main method is farming 10 "souls" of almost any monster to unlock it as a pet/mount; souls also drop from the Shugo Shop and the Black Cloud Merchant, and rare mounts can come from Hidden Cubes ⟦1⟧.

d33e6853.en: The in-game Pets menu has a "Source" tab showing exactly where a given soul drops.

4b116fd7.en: Beginner priority: don't ignore world mobs while leveling, many double as free future mounts once you've collected 10 souls; check the Source tab before grinding blindly for a specific pet.

2e18ce5b.en: Flight is a real combat mechanic, not cosmetic; wings and mounts are complementary tools.

94707fd0.en: Flight is a core combat and traversal mechanic, not just cosmetic transportation; some Abyss boss mechanics reportedly require flight to execute correctly. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

e9301dfe.en: Wings are not available from level 1; one single, unverified source gives a rough unlock around level 10.

795b7512.en: Wings have a "flight power" stat acting as airborne stamina; upgrading a wing raises max flight power via a physics-based "Glide Gauge" rather than a rigid timer ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

92c6f588.en: Only wings earned through gameplay grant flight power; purchased cosmetic wing skins sit in a separate skin slot layered over your earned wings and provide no flight benefit ⟦1⟧.

0a0d7849.en: Higher-quality wings also add flat Attack/Defense/HP and can grant movement speed or special combat effects.

336f2c9b.en: Beginner priority: use mounts as your short-range sprint tool and wings/gliding as your long-range terrain-skip tool, they're complementary, not redundant. Manage your Glide Gauge deliberately, since running out mid-air just drops you.

ccfd01c2.en: Legions cap at 128 members and offer organization and group access; the level, hall and buff perks below are disputed.

1d3033bf.en: AION 2's guild system, capped at up to 128 members per Legion, used for PvE, PvP, crafting, and social access. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ Legion perks are mostly about organization and access to reliable groups rather than direct stat buffs. ⟦3⟧

b7bc3482.en: Legion Hall unlocks at Legion level 5, costs 1,000,000 Kinah to rent, and houses cooking, alchemy, jewelcrafting, armorsmithing, and blacksmithing merchants/workbenches together, the real convenience benefit ⟦1⟧.

973d6d99.en: Legion Coin is earned for active contribution and spent on Legion-exclusive skins, uniforms, masks, mounts, and wings at specialized merchants ⟦1⟧.

46dce0d4.en: Legion levels beyond 5 raise the member cap and unlock member access to purchase or use new Abyss weapons and armor ⟦1⟧.

ba4d9420.en: Disputed: the Legion level, Legion Hall unlock and Abyss-gear perks above come from a single boosting-adjacent source. Three independent sources say Legions have no levels, warehouse or mechanical buffs, and a developer statement from February 2026 agrees. See the "Legion: Rank Structure and the Warehouse/Buff Controversy" card further down this page.

9db70134.en: Beginner priority: join an active Legion early for group content access and Legion Hall crafting convenience; don't expect membership itself to be a large stat boost.

2fd4c0b8.en: There's no universal companion system, only the Spiritmaster's four elemental summon spirits.

8ae06562.en: There is no evidence of a general, class-agnostic "companion" or "summon" progression system in AION 2.

b558be35.en: The only summon-type mechanic found is class-specific to the Spiritmaster, which channels four elemental spirits (Fire, Water, Wind, Earth) as combat pets/turrets with independent attack capability, used to chain skill activations for DPS. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

f8f44b10.en: Treat "Companions" as not a universal system; it is a Spiritmaster kit feature, not something every character has.

61ea36e9.en: PvE and PvP stats are fully separate

5992d264.en: PvE and PvP stats are fully separate pools; build your PvE set first and ignore PvP caps for now.

839b1c3a.en: Accuracy governs the chance to land an attack and, per one source, also affects crit chance; Precision is a hybrid stat raising both Accuracy and Crit chance. ⟦1⟧

ee87de4b.en: PvE Attack/Defense only comes from PvE gear and only affects damage to monsters; PvP Attack/Defense only comes from PvP gear and only affects damage to other players ⟦1⟧.

63483002.en: One source states endgame PvE targets are roughly Accuracy 2350 and Critical Hit 2600-2700 depending on synergy/buffs. ⟦1⟧

0f60531b.en: The Combat Power formula itself stops rewarding further Accuracy above 1700 or Crit above 80%, making stacking past those levels inefficient for Combat Power purposes.

f5ca678b.en: Because burst damage is high (one source claims an Assassin can deal about 80% of a target's HP in one combo), the recommended early PvP stat order is HP, crit resistance, mitigation, then PvP Defense. ⟦1⟧

e2d04eee.en: PvP Attack is added only once survival is established.

a1c8a827.en: Beginner priority: build one PvE stat set first and don't chase PvP stat caps until you're actually PvPing regularly.

ba61ad06.en: Entry tickets removed as of Jul 2026 patch

8c652133.en: Odyle Energy opens reward cubes after a clear, not dungeon entry, and it's shared across normal and Transcendence runs.

df83a23d.en: Transcendence is AION 2's endgame progression/ranking layer, class-ranked, fed by specific dungeons such as "Phantom Corridor" with up to 4 escalating difficulty levels that raise the minimum entry Combat Power and monster strength; main rewards are Arcana cards plus Breakthrough Stone Fragments and Stigma Shard Fragments (single source, KR-era).

4ad72cb7.en: As of a July 1, 2026 patch, entry tickets for Expedition and Transcendence dungeons were removed; instead, Odyle Energy is spent only to open the reward cube after clearing a run. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

e85cb18f.en: A normal boss cube costs 40 energy and Hard difficulty costs 60, and normal/Transcendence dungeons draw from the same shared energy pool.

27234f75.en: One source states Transcendence content becomes available around gear score ~1650, unverified elsewhere ⟦1⟧.

436cd457.en: No evidence was found of a traditional "class advancement" or ascension tier in AION 2.

d6bdacb8.en: What exists instead is Transcendence dungeons plus "Awakening Battles," timed solo encounters with extra objectives and temporary combat bonuses, a separate activity track from Episode/Region/Mission content (single source, could not verify further).

fd96f164.en: Beginner priority: entry itself isn't gated by energy, so you can scout Transcendence dungeons early, but budget your Odyle Energy between normal and Transcendence content since they share one pool.

54f123e7.en: Five professions, gathering feeds all of them

4780423e.en: Five crafting professions share one gathering skill; pick one or two rather than spreading thin.

8ae9631e.en: Five primary crafting professions are cited: Blacksmithing, Armor Smithing, Handicrafting, Alchemy, and Cooking. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ Cooking produces food/drink buffs used before dungeons and PvP.

f0501a01.en: Gathering is done via an "Essence Extraction" skill/action used to mine ore, gather herbs, or cut wood, feeding all five crafting lines.

7dc2a3c1.en: No evidence found of a dedicated dyeing system; classic AION had player-dye mechanics, so its absence here is flagged as unverified rather than confirmed absent.

b32f5a27.en: Beginner priority: pick one or two gathering skills that match your intended crafting profession rather than spreading thin, and use the Legion Hall once available (Legion level 5) to access all five crafting stations in one place ⟦1⟧.

21e987be.en: AION 2 gates dungeon rewards, not dungeon entry, behind a stamina-like energy pool. This guide walks through what that energy does, the full list of dungeon types, and where to spend limited energy at each stage of leveling.

6db8fd41.en: Because global has not launched, almost every specific number below comes from the KR/TW live client and should be treated as subject to change at the October 5, 2026 global release.

b1661aea.en: Energy only gates reward cubes, not dungeon entry; spend it daily so it never caps out.

93431607.en: The core resource is a stamina-like pool that gates dungeon reward claiming, not dungeon entry itself. Energy does not block entering or clearing a dungeon; it only gates opening the final reward cube at the end.

ce1719bc.en: Running a dungeon with insufficient energy still lets you clear it, just with no loot from that cube. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

0f668c61.en: Naming is inconsistent across English fan sites: "Odell Energy," "Odyle Energy," "Odile Energy," and "Aetherine Energy" all appear to refer to the same underlying system, which the Korean community calls Od Energy. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧.

80f26193.en: Opening a boss/reward cube costs 40 energy, cited consistently for high-level Conquest and Transcendence dungeons ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧.

29549fac.en: Multiple sources give a maximum cap of 560 energy, beyond which passive regeneration stops and overflow is wasted ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

36961cb5.en: Base regen is cited as 15 energy every 3 hours by u4n, but a Korean source states this already includes a 50% membership bonus, implying a non-member base rate closer to 10 per 3 hours. ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

31ac6ef1.en: That's roughly 80/day, about 560/week, which would make "560" possibly a weekly-accumulation figure as much as a hard cap.

4dc7582c.en: The same Korean source states total weekly Od Energy obtainable is 1,400, broken down as: ⟦1⟧

8139dfb8.en: Base passive charge with membership: about 840/week

19a71699.en: Small unreliable drops from faction quests, field orders, and Abyss orders

aac330e4.en: Players can craft energy-restoring stones, capped at 7 per week, each restoring 40 energy ⟦1⟧.

566b52f9.en: Normal/Exploration dungeons, Party dungeons, and Transcendence dungeons all draw from the same energy pool, there is no separate currency per dungeon type ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

6850a71e.en: Membership tiers increase the charge rate by 50%, increase the Odyle Energy Cube Selection Count in Expedition/Transcendence/Sanctuary content, and double weekly Abyss access hours ⟦1⟧.

c4a4b591.en: One source states characters begin generating this energy at level 22 ⟦1⟧.

b2280e9e.en: Separate from energy, individual dungeon types also carry their own entry-count limits, such as 7 entries per week for Daily/Party dungeons, expandable via purchasable tickets. ⟦1⟧

05b09300.en: Energy and entry counts are two separate gating systems that both apply at once.

b88f6a7d.en: Auto-hunt/expedition energy draw is unverified: no source confirms or denies whether open-world auto-hunt consumes this pool.

bf9d8faa.en: Beginner priority: spend energy daily so it never sits at the cap, since regen stops there and future income is lost; never spend it on a weak reward pool relative to your current gear bottleneck.

e377f502.en: Common mistake: letting energy sit at the cap while questing, which wastes ongoing regeneration.

7b6b6ec9.en: AION 2 does not have a true built-in AFK auto-battle system comparable to mobile MMOs. The combat design is action-oriented, positioning, timing, interrupts, which works against passive AFK play ⟦1⟧.

45a5dc57.en: Some players use the in-game macro system plus auto-target to semi-automate stationary grinding, holding or spamming one key while multitasking, but this is not fully hands-off.

30874d52.en: Do not confuse AION 2 with original AION's later-patch "auto hunting" feature, that is a different game.

d9ef44a7.en: No source found documents specific AFK/grinding spots by level range, nor confirms whether energy is consumed by any auto-hunt mechanic, since no full auto-hunt mechanic was confirmed to exist at all. Treat this whole sub-topic as largely unverified pending global launch.

8840f9cf.en: Avoid: planning around AFK auto-hunt as a leveling strategy.

969f7e01.en: Groups run the classic Tank/Healer/DPS trinity plus an optional flex support slot.

f102e90c.en: Group content uses the classic MMO trinity, Tank, Healer, DPS, with an optional flex/support slot in 4-player content. A Party Finder matchmaking tool supports role-based filtering and difficulty selection ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

2aec2b6c.en: Tank: pace based on the healer's capacity, group mobs tightly for AoE, use defensive cooldowns proactively ⟦1⟧.

9104528e.en: Healer: use efficient/cheap heals by default, save big cooldowns for genuine danger, track debuffs, communicate pace.

62206c46.en: DPS: focus priority targets, take assigned interrupts, prioritize survival/uptime over raw parse numbers, "clean mechanics and uptime beat big numbers."

eac894e0.en: Give a short heads-up on your first run, "please call out the important mechanic," it's considered useful, not a burden.

ab5bae85.en: Agree on loot rules (roll for valuable items, need = immediate equip, greed = materials) before the first pull.

3c89a3ee.en: Start a pull while someone is reading a tooltip, respeccing, or returning from a release.

f5a6e5bc.en: Change loot rules mid-run once they're agreed.

5505064a.en: Propose a different fix from everyone after a wipe, agree on one single adjustment instead.

d14c4d48.en: Chase speed for its own sake as tank, "your job is not to go as fast as possible... without dying."

979f64fd.en: Flex/Support in 4-player content provides interrupts, crowd control, dispels, and emergency buffs as a fifth utility role. BoostRoom and similar sites (u4n, mmoexp, expcarry, timesaver.gg, LDCloud) sell currency/boosting/carry services; treat any "buy X" framing as marketing, not neutral advice, though the etiquette content itself is generic MMO best practice.

bef99a23.ctx: money / Money: what to buy, what to skip

a910f923.en: AION 2 global is free to play, but a $15/month Membership gates the player economy, and Founder's Packs, a per-character battle pass, and a cosmetics shop all compete for your wallet. This panel ranks what is actually worth buying for a beginner.
a910f923.ctx: money / Money: what to buy, what to skip

da78846b.en: On sale now, one per account

7c9d38e0.en: Buy Standard if you're playing at launch; skip Deluxe and Ultimate unless you want the skins.

2b012a0d.en: Three tiers are on sale now on Steam and NC PURPLE. Only one purchase is allowed per account, and Steam does not let you upgrade to a higher tier later. PURPLE reportedly offers separate upgrade products. ⟦1⟧

8e1a1f97.en: 5 days Advance Access (Sept 30 to Oct 4, 2026), 30-day Membership, one Daeva's Campaign Supply Chest, "Vanguard of Atreia" title

2be2d5ad.en: Everything in Standard, plus "Ascended Daeva" armor skin and "Eternal Sun" weapon skin

c808a093.en: Everything in Deluxe, plus Daeva's Styling Chest, "Moonlit Aria" armor skin, Black Dragon pet, Blazing Sun wings

91e439e2.en: Prices and contents cross-checked across sources ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧

75bd4ff1.en: Skip: Deluxe and Ultimate, unless you specifically want the cosmetic skins, pet, or wings. Zero functional gain over Standard.

40b1e8bb.en: Unlocks the Kina to Quna Exchange, converting earned gold into premium currency

bd7322cc.en: Beginner tip: a casual player trying the game can skip it. Anyone planning to trade, gear up seriously, or play past the early levels will likely feel pressure to subscribe once trading and currency conversion matter. ⟦1⟧

7d952ea2.en: Quna: premium currency, bought with real money or obtained by converting Kina through the Membership-gated Exchange

Consumables (potions, resurrection stones) are stated to "not affect gear progression or long-term power" and are "also earnable through regular gameplay." ⟦1⟧

4e5ff903.en: Skip unless you want the specific skins.

507766b0.en: Save upgrade materials, skip the pricier Abyss scrolls, and don't over-invest in gear you'll replace.

4e40cc91.en: Selling or discarding gear-upgrade materials (enhancement fragments) instead of saving them. They are scarce once early one-time quests are used up confirmed, 2+ sources ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

cb0b2971.en: Ignoring cheaper "grey" Abyss scroll options at weekly vendors that give identical rewards to pricier variants single source ⟦1⟧.

1948b532.en: Prioritizing low-value daily dungeon rewards (pets, Kinah) over enhancement stones needed for gear progression single source ⟦1⟧.

d1664f37.en: Avoid: grabbing the shiny reward over the one that actually feeds your gear pipeline.

bfe0671b.en: Enhancing gear you will replace soon, wasting scarce upgrade materials on temporary items confirmed, 2+ sources ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

4bb074aa.en: Don't spend keys early, skip valuable daily quests, or attempt weekly content before you're ready.

68e3db4c.en: Spending limited daily keys (for example, Shugo Fiesta) before reaching max level, which reduces their endgame value. single source ⟦1⟧

0521c340.en: Picking the wrong daily quests and missing ones that reward valuable bound keys or fragments. single source ⟦1⟧

e115af46.en: Attempting the Ascension Trial or other high-end weekly content before meeting its real item-level requirement, wasting a limited weekly attempt.

c32d1b77.en: Avoid: guessing your readiness, check item level and combat power against the requirement first.

44a4521b.en: Avoiding the Abyss/PvP entirely. Non-PvP players can still earn Abyss points through supply quests and PvE kills, which feed gear and Stigma systems single source ⟦1⟧.

b2f49891.en: Playing with no weekly plan at all. Repeatedly called out as the single biggest efficiency mistake, since weekly caps and high-value activities matter more than hours logged confirmed, 2+ sources ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

1306338d.en: Misusing macros in ways that risk an account flag, stick to the sanctioned two-skill auto-attack macro rather than third-party automation single source.

271dcbd1.en: Over-grinding materials using outdated KR-original farming routes once global numbers differ single source.

29a53e7e.en: Don't grind blind: mix in side content, commit to one build, and confirm skill slots and item level vs combat power.

e7258e0a.en: Leveling purely through grinding and XP while ignoring side content, arriving at cap under-geared and under-built confirmed, 2+ sources ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

c0de617b.en: Confusing item level with combat power and misjudging whether you can actually clear a dungeon confirmed, 2+ sources ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

8284b3c3.en: Unlocking a skill effect but forgetting to manually slot it, the effect does not apply until assigned single source ⟦1⟧.

c33bfdd5.en: Avoid: assuming an unlocked skill effect is automatically active, check your skill slots.

37b581ce.en: Spreading Skill Points and Stigma resources across too many builds instead of committing to one coherent PvE or PvP setup first confirmed, 2+ sources ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

7acf20e4.en: Not tracking your own progress or metrics, which makes it hard to tell whether your routine is actually working versus the game simply being grindy single source ⟦1⟧.

582976e1.en: Avoid taking any of this as settled: every tier and difficulty claim in this table is KR/TW-era, gathered before global launch and before any global balance pass. Several rest on boosting or carry-service tier lists marketing rather than independent testing, and even the more data-driven leaderboard source only reflects the KR/TW live meta, not global. Treat every ranking here as a snapshot that may already be stale by the October 5, 2026 global launch.

7c775a30.en: If you might want to swap classes later: none of the beginner-overview research for this guide documents a way to change an existing character's class, so switching later in practice means leveling a new character, an alt. Two facts from that research matter here. First, per-character systems including the Daeva Pass, Stigma builds, and gear do not share progress across characters, so trying a second class means rebuilding all of that from zero ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧. Second, once an account registers 84 combined dungeon clears within a single weekly lockout, tradeable Kinah and gear drops are reduced, one source says by 90 percent, for the rest of that week across every character on the account, not just the one that hit the threshold ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧. In practice, rolling one or two alts to try a different class looks fine; heavily dungeon-farming your main and a would-be replacement class in the same week is exactly the pattern that penalty targets.

e965ccbe.en: No single guide gives a definitive numbered Skill Point leveling order for Templar, unlike the more detailed Gladiator guides. The list below is assembled from pieces documented across sources; treat it as single source or contested unless noted.

c00949f4.en: Do first: chain Vicious Strike to build and hold aggro, your bread-and-butter threat generator confirmed ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

78c037e8.en: Do first: Provoke, a single-target taunt used to lock a boss's aggro onto yourself confirmed ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

ac0290a5.en: Do first: Doom Shield, a defensive and mitigation cooldown, timed against confirmed incoming burst rather than used on cooldown confirmed ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

6a772b1b.en: Then: Punishment and Decisive Strike, hard-hitting follow-ups used once a target is locked down. Punishment is also described elsewhere as a chargeable AoE with lifesteal in an endgame raid-tank build single source ⟦1⟧.

1eb67fb1.en: Then, for mob packs: Flash Cut (2s cooldown, hits 3 targets, usable while moving) triggers Bloodsword Slash, which heals for 100% of damage dealt single source ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

4367c31b.en: Then, for mob packs: Trial (also called Falling Sword Spirits) hits up to 6 targets and reduces their defense by 30% single source ⟦1⟧.

68fe140d.en: Then, for mob packs: Shield Strike grants a shield and heals more the more enemies it hits single source ⟦1⟧.

9b077000.en: Then: Capture pulls a target up to 20m in and binds it 2 to 3 seconds, with a 100% bind chance on NPCs, good for consolidating scattered mobs before an AoE mitigation skill single source (community synthesis, no direct link)

1e252512.en: Later / optional: fund whichever mitigation or taunt skill you actually have equipped in your active rotation over situational or off-role skills; no source names specific Templar skills to ignore early ⟦1⟧.

07281627.en: contested, KR-era, single source A Korean forum post about 수호성 (Templar) passives gives two competing rankings for five named passives: 격앙 (Fury), 모욕의 포효 (Roar of Insult), 충격 적중 (Impact Hit), 체력 강화 (HP boost), 단죄의 가호 (Judgment's Grace), and 철벽 방어 (Iron Wall Defense).

6dd9b428.en: By felt or practical value: Fury > Roar of Insult > Impact Hit, with the rest called not worth investing in

cadbbb7f.en: By raw combat-power-per-level the order flips: Iron Wall Defense (+0.356k) > Impact Hit (+0.244k) > HP boost (+0.233k) > Judgment's Grace (+0.111k) > Fury (+0.078k); Fury's felt value beats its CP number ⟦1⟧

be1742b7.en: A second, independent KR guide broadly agrees on prioritizing core damage or defense passives over utility ones, but does not give the same explicit order single source ⟦1⟧

c2d50225.en: Gap remains: the two rankings above disagree with each other (felt value vs. raw CP-per-level), and neither maps cleanly onto the English passive names used elsewhere on this page, so treat this as a starting point, not a settled order.

f9aa793b.en: Role: Melee DPS with off-tank flex. Difficulty: Forgiving to learn, but early levels can feel sluggish. Weapon: Greatsword or Polearm.

46a63748.en: Gladiator is a forgiving, self-sustaining melee DPS that can flex into off-tank duty.

4c1d013a.en: The Gladiator is AION 2's heavy melee DPS with meaningful off-tank capability, wielding two-handed weapons: a Greatsword or a Polearm confirmed ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

eabf466d.en: In Korean the class is referred to as 검성, roughly "sword saint." Korean community threads on Inven's 검성 board match the Gladiator's kit and confirm the KR name mapping single source ⟦1⟧.

14deab1b.en: AION2 Hub lists the kit at 52 total skills, 43 active and 9 passive single source ⟦1⟧; a separate fetch of the class page gave 40 active/9 passive for the same 52 total contested on the active count, same domain ⟦2⟧.

1ee04aca.en: Pitched as one of the more forgiving melee classes to learn, thanks to a simple, rhythm-based playstyle built around basic attacks and lifesteal sustain rather than tight execution windows single source ⟦1⟧

e55aa9f9.en: High HP pool lets it flex into an off-tank/secondary-tank role in group content even though its primary job is frontline DPS confirmed ⟦1⟧

74a866a5.en: PvE standing (KR/TW meta): strong for dungeons and boss fights via sustained AoE damage and self-healing, and can function as a sub-tank when geared for it single source ⟦1⟧.

8bdf5f6b.en: KR-era, pre-launch feedback: focus-group testers reportedly found the class "slow and clunky" with skills that "felt weak and lacked impact" prior to a rebalance pass, and multiple sources agree the class "transforms" once mid-game gear, animations, and cooldown mastery come online contested-but-consistent, two independent sources ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧. Balance patches may have already addressed this by TW/global launch.

69ee637d.en: Excels in frontline skirmishes and small-scale fights (1v1, 2v2) thanks to burst damage, mobility, and CC tools, with success depending heavily on timing and positioning rather than pure stats single source ⟦1⟧

c9b6cff5.en: LepreStore's role-based tier framing places Gladiator as combining "strong PvP with durability and useful party buffs" rather than ranking it in a strict S-F tier single source ⟦1⟧

2f927205.en: Party demand: solid as a melee DPS that can flex to off-tank duty in a pinch, though no source gave a hard queue-priority figure.

6c7d6ba3.en: Best for players who want a durable, self-sustaining melee class that rewards positioning and cluster-hitting over precise combo execution, and who want a class that is comparatively forgiving for solo leveling single source ⟦1⟧.

4b8ef2f1.en: Two KR guides partly disagree; Attack Preparation is the one passive every source agrees is critical.

241ab789.en: Two independent Vortex Gaming write-ups give partially overlapping, partially conflicting PvE skill priorities. Both are KR-era.

08cfbf9e.en: Then: Charge Strike, Shatter Wave, Ankle Cut, Leap Strike

b0d0e7a9.en: Later: Armor of Balance, Zikel's Blessing, Assault Stance

69ff8819.en: Do first: Survival Stance, called strong for both PvP and PvE

a2d583c0.en: Then: Sharp Separation (three specializations, or spirit/MP recovery if mana is tight), Slam of Severance (movement-skill change plus critical-hit MP recovery)

36c6d6bf.en: Then: Leap Strike (combat-readiness effect matters, recast reset useful for grinding), Strike Down (specialize for action-immune targets, guarantees a critical hit at skill level 20)

a6a44956.en: Then: Crushing Wave, recast reset on critical hit rated essential

bae678ab.en: Deprioritize: Armor of Protection and Damage Absorption, citing low efficiency from long recast times

7b84a564.en: 예리한 일격 (Sharp Strike / Keen Strike): non-targeted, move-while-casting hit that builds threat and restores MP; level to 12

7bf44ee0.en: 절단의 맹타 (Cleaving Fierce Strike): AoE hit that raises threat and the Groggy gauge; also level to 12 single source ⟦1⟧

14e95a3e.en: Attack Preparation (공격 준비, raises Attack Power and Defense): repeatedly called the single most important passive across both English and Korean sources confirmed ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

be880236.en: Veteran Counter: amplifies damage after a successful block; recommended to be maxed out single source ⟦1⟧

72d115d1.en: Weakness Analysis (약점 파악, raises critical hit rate and Perfect stat) and Blood Absorption (피의 흡수, lifesteal on hit) round out the recommended passive set single source ⟦1⟧

e2b388c5.en: Skills to ignore early: Armor of Protection and Damage Absorption per priority order 2 above; treat as single-source/contested since priority order 1 does not mention either skill.

26de77fd.en: Mastery/chain skills: Strike Down is a chain enabler against action-immune (staggered) targets and a guaranteed-crit finisher once specialized to level 20 single source ⟦1⟧.

b20d5cc1.en: Max Sharp Strike, then push Cleaving Fierce Strike to skill Lv 12 before passives; Zikel's Blessing is the first Stigma.

ed372a1e.en: This order comes from Korean Gladiator (검성) community threads on Inven, corroborated by a KR blog ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧. Every number below is the skill's own internal level (its 8/12/16/20/25 breakpoint), not your character level, unless a step says otherwise.

40df8176.en: keeps sustain and mana up while grinding

017a8d60.en: most recommended skill to push to 12 first

450f8434.en: Then max, in order: Blood Absorption (피의 흡수), Attack Preparation (공격 준비), Weakness Analysis (약점 파악) ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

f725f544.en: Max Sharp Strike, push Cleaving Fierce Strike to skill Lv 12, then dump into passives

0942f19c.en: This leveling-phase order comes from Inven's Gladiator board, corroborated by redwendy's write-up ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

d2f1172f.en: Stigma unlocks: slot Zikel's Blessing first

475ba22a.en: Every source that names a first-priority PVE stigma names Zikel's Blessing (지켈의 축복) ⟦1⟧. See the note below before slotting a second.

8701b805.en: Hand-off: push the PVE core 3 to skill Lv 20

e23fe756.en: Downward Strike, Cleaving Fierce Strike, and Destruction Slash become the mandatory endgame trio ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

688a6e02.en: Then Shatter Wave or Yurin's Blade, to taste

8bff9440.en: Both paths come from the same 2026-02-02 thread, the most detailed step order found for this class ⟦1⟧; treat skill Lv 20 as the target state to grow into once Skill Points are in surplus, not a leveling order. See Skill priority above and Stigma picks below for the rest of the endgame spread.

30500bf4.en: No separate "Leave at level 1" list: the only level-1 pick the note supports is Fury Wave, a Stigma skill covered in the warning below. No "Gear while leveling" block either, since the note found no reliable source for level-specific gear or weapon-swap breakpoints for this class.

3b57876d.en: Assault Stance (돌격 자세) is called a fixed level-20 or level-25 stigma pick by three sources ⟦1⟧, but a separate PVE-focused thread excludes it entirely, calling it inferior to support-synergy picks ⟦2⟧. Treat its PVE value as contested, not confirmed.

bca49d23.en: Avoid: pushing Fury Wave (분노의 파동) past Stigma level 1; it only matters for its basic Groggy-trigger effect, and higher levels are called low-return ⟦1⟧.

44be763f.en: Max Assault Stance and Zikel's Blessing first; they repeat as top picks across every source.

7599eeb8.en: Greater Stigma slots unlock via group quests around level 45 to 50

763920e0.en: Normal Stigma Skills cap at level 20 on base shards

9bf412e6.en: kr-era, subject to change at global launch The Korean service has since raised the cap to 25, with up to six Stigmas equippable at once ⟦1⟧

9a41e6ef.en: Armor of Balance, Zikel's Blessing, Assault Stance, Block, Path Explosion

b1163825.en: Enhancement priority: level Path Explosion to 15 (max 20 if resources allow), Armor of Balance to level 20

3e3490c7.en: Assault Stance, Zikel's Blessing (called essential, +50% Danite hit chance), Focused Block, Blade Wind, Perseverance

8eab65d4.en: Blade Toss (mandatory, 40% healing reduction plus a 50% base effect), Tenacity (3-second survival window), Assault Stance (also resets Tenacity's cooldown), Forced Bind (combo enabler)

753e341a.en: Assault Stance, Armor of Balance, Blade Wind, Siege

108e3a1b.en: Korean community consensus: 지켈 (Zikel's Blessing) and 돌격 자세 (Assault Stance) are both worth maxing to stigma level 25 for PvE and PvP alike, with Assault Stance as the top pick to invest in first; fill remaining slots to taste after that single source ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

35a1d069.en: What to spend Stigma Shards on first: across every Gladiator source, Assault Stance and Zikel's Blessing are the two names that repeat as first priority confirmed pattern, three independent sources, consistent with the general system advice to fund whatever you actually have equipped over situational alternates ⟦1⟧.

682abc91.en: No official Gladiator route exists; community guidance says invest in active-skill nodes first.

e8751463.en: single source, KR-era, community synthesis not an official guide Community synthesis recommends investing in blue (active-skill-level) nodes first, starting from the board's start node (S) and pushing toward whichever aggressive DPS-increasing nodes are reachable without breaking the connection chain ⟦1⟧.

fa419b68.en: Early on, only the basic attack and always-on skill plus one need to be opened to play comfortably. A forum thread on Nezekan-board point optimization for Gladiator corroborates the "actives first" approach without adding new detail single source ⟦1⟧.

a9d63fe7.en: Daevanion Points buy nodes on a shared board; nodes add either flat combat stats or extra levels to specific skills. Points come from normal leveling plus Daevanion Crystals from quests and achievements.

2b17dcee.en: Strategy: path to the nearest node that actually helps your loadout and treat filler connector nodes as a toll, not a destination. Damage-focused builds like Gladiator's should weight uptime and output nodes over pure survival nodes: "damage builds value uptime and output... tanks value control and survival" ⟦1⟧.

6f89d54f.en: kr-era Reset costs 500 Kinah per individual node in the Korean client; cost may differ at global launch ⟦1⟧. No reliable source found on when specifically a Gladiator should reset.

341c086c.en: No confirmed Arcana list for Gladiator; a Chalice/Parchment/Compass/Paper/Mirror set is documented.

cd7ecce1.en: Recommended Arcana types for Gladiator/Swordmaster: Chalice, Parchment, Compass, Paper, and Mirror single source, search-synthesized ⟦1⟧.

153e1163.en: Chalice: Vitality Chalice recommended, prioritize the Strike Down and Crushing Wave slots.

eb60beaf.en: Parchment: Strike Down treated as essential, with Slam of Destruction and Sharp Strike as secondary picks.

70dcacf1.en: Compass: Slam of Severance and Crushing Wave essential, followed by Violate Sword, Dashing Strike, Sword Aura Tree, and Impact Release.

2b3745eb.en: Paper: a Mana-type Paper is recommended for increased destructive power, paired with raising Attack Preparation.

200a0363.en: Mirror: Veteran Counter and Exploit Weakness are the priority effects; the specific card name for Mirror was not given in the source.

45856585.en: For newer players building a general Arcana set rather than min-maxing per skill, a Frenzy 4 / Purity 2 set is recommended, described as easier to build and giving strong early PvE scaling into higher-level Transcendence content single source ⟦1⟧.

92507db9.en: Arcana cards to avoid: two independent Korean community threads warn against making a Unique-grade Arcana card out of 검기 난무 (Sword Aura Rampage) or 파멸의 맹타 (Ruin's Fierce Strike), calling it something players will regret; they instead insist the Chalice (성배) card must be built around 내려찍기 (Downward Strike) kr-era single source per claim, two threads agree ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

997ab1fb.en: Separately, on the newer Arcana set additions, the 수호 (Guardian) and 불굴 (Indomitable) sets are framed as PvP-oriented and 징벌 (Punishment) as PvE-oriented, implying a Gladiator PvE build should avoid over-investing in the Guardian/Indomitable sets kr-era single source ⟦1⟧.

5e86ef05.en: Greatsword for PvE stability, Polearm for PvP burst; stack Attack Power, Crit, and Lifesteal.

b41a81fb.en: Weapon type: Greatsword is described as the more balanced choice, favored for PvE stability and AoE chains; Polearm offers longer reach and higher burst, favored for PvP duels and crowd fights confirmed, two independent sources ⟦1⟧.

80a9b825.en: Stat priority, contested between two sources:

1687a485.en: Then: Lifesteal, called essential for the self-healing bruiser playstyle

3edea69a.en: Then: Attack Speed, called critical for smoothing out the early-game feel

d6fff445.en: Later / bulk: Defense and HP as secondary bulk stats

c342cc3e.en: Offense: Weapon Damage, Attack Boost, Critical Damage, frontal/cleave damage

77b80450.en: Both orderings are broadly consistent; treat the exact ranking as contested between the two.

7a8fbe3b.en: Which piece to enhance first: most damage dealers, Gladiator included, are advised to enhance their weapon first before investing deeply in armor single source ⟦1⟧.

76f324f9.en: Set effects and gear names (KR-era, may not map 1:1)

6299c111.en: kr-era, names may not map 1:1 to global localization Recommended gear names from a KR guide single source ⟦1⟧:

354bfbd2.en: Nua armor set: recommended for PvE only; PvP-oriented gear also serves hybrid builds.

f42a506d.en: Gunyongwang accessory set: recommended for PvE, or alternatively upgrade Abyss (PvP-zone) accessories instead.

5f232a11.en: Black Dragon Greatsword for PvE; what the guide calls a "Rin Sword" for PvP.

ddd67c90.en: A crafted "Garder" (belt-slot item, exact translation uncertain), tuned for Power, Combat Speed, and Danite Hit.

aea3a610.en: Translation caution: the "Rin Sword" name reads as a possible localization/translation artifact given Gladiator's greatsword/polearm kit, so treat it with extra caution.

9118f2b2.en: Manastone or godstone equivalents: no AION 2-specific manastone or godstone terminology was found. The Arcana/Key/Hourglass system documented above appears to be the closest analog, but no source explicitly confirmed the mapping from AION 1's manastone/godstone system.

00f2a8d3.en: Open with Assault Stance, chain AoE into finishers, and save lifesteal skills for right after big hits.

8b42cf81.en: Beginner PvE rotation, synthesizing the two Vortex Gaming skill-priority lists:

6c05d523.en: Open with Assault Stance for the combat-speed and MP-cost buff.

eb733644.en: Weave in Sharp Strike / 예리한 일격 periodically to keep MP topped up between bigger hits.

c2d7d6d2.en: Lead with your AoE knockdown, Charge Strike, Path Explosion, or Shatter Wave depending on which build you're following, to group and stagger enemies.

64edc12f.en: Follow with single-target finishers, Strike Down, Ankle Cut, Leap Strike, on priority or action-immune targets.

019b893a.en: Close with Crushing Wave once its recast has been reset by a critical hit confirmed pattern ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

bf7f9fb0.en: Key chain combos: Forced Bind into Downward Strike as a PvP setup-into-burst combo, and Path Explosion (knockdown) into Downward Strike as an alternate opener when Forced Bind is unavailable. Blade Toss doubles as a farming or poke damage tool outside of combo windows single source ⟦1⟧.

c705fc1a.en: Macro setup documented for auto-hunt or quick execution: a macro bound to Blade of Severance, with Sharp Strike, Sword Dance, Path Explosion, and Downward Strike all linked to a single left-click input for streamlined execution single source ⟦1⟧.

ef3f3380.en: Blood Smash (or "Lifestealing Blade" in another source's naming) converts roughly 15% of damage dealt into HP. It's recommended as a reactive tool, used right after taking a big hit or during a burst trade rather than spammed on cooldown, since its value comes from timing, not uptime single source ⟦1⟧.

7fc7a57e.en: Korean community advice reinforces this for AoE survival specifically: dropping 분쇄파동 (Shatter/Crushing Wave) into the center of a mob cluster heals you sharply in proportion to how many enemies it hits, a panic-button sustain tool when surrounded single source ⟦1⟧.

5ddc6160.en: Gladiator levels fast and safe: strong AoE clear plus lifesteal sustain, though early levels feel slow.

56e806d0.en: Solo leveling comfort: high. Multiple independent sources describe Gladiator as one of the most stable and forgiving melee classes to solo-level, citing consistent AoE clearing plus reliable lifesteal sustain confirmed ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

657c8548.en: Sustain is primarily lifesteal-based: the Blood Absorption passive plus active skills like Blood Smash/Lifestealing Blade convert a percentage of damage into HP, rather than relying on potions or mana regen.

79a82853.en: Sustain scales with landing hits on multiple enemies at once, so positioning for cluster hits directly improves survivability confirmed, same sources.

5b1034eb.en: Mob density tips: the class is explicitly built to wade into mob clusters and clear them with sweeping AoE while healing off the damage dealt; learning enemy spawn and movement patterns to strike during cluster moments is called out as the core solo-leveling skill for this class single source ⟦1⟧.

36bdbc1e.en: KR-era, pre-launch feedback: early levels reportedly feel sluggish and low-impact based on focus-test feedback, but the class is consistently described as transforming in the mid-game once better animations, tighter combos, and cooldown mastery come online contested-but-consistent ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧. Later balance passes may have changed this.

17e61294.en: Learn to dodge, weave basic attacks for MP, and enhance your weapon before armor.

6bde9890.en: Assuming heavy armor lets you tank hits without needing to dodge; learning dodge timing is called out as one of the biggest power spikes a new Gladiator player can unlock single source ⟦1⟧.

ccd4d1ef.en: Poor MP management from spamming skills instead of weaving basic attacks and Sharp Strike (예리한 일격) to keep mana topped up confirmed, English and Korean sources ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

82200bf8.en: Over-investing scarce upgrade materials into starting gear before learning core combat and movement fundamentals single source ⟦1⟧.

412d575c.en: Not prioritizing the weapon slot for enhancement, when weapon level drives most of a DPS class's damage output single source, same guide ⟦1⟧.

b731973b.en: Spamming lifesteal skills (Blood Smash/Lifestealing Blade) on cooldown instead of saving them for immediately after a big hit or during a burst trade, which wastes their sustain value single source ⟦1⟧.

1db5a901.en: Ignoring positioning for AoE cluster hits, not baiting or gathering mobs into cleave range before committing an AoE skill single source ⟦1⟧.

7eff88d8.en: Neglecting the Attack Preparation and Veteran Counter passives, which multiple sources call the class's most important scaling passives, in favor of leveling only active skills confirmed ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

a5e33a06.en: Picking Greatsword or Polearm without matching the choice to intended content (Greatsword for PvE stability, Polearm for PvP reach/burst), then being surprised the weapon doesn't fit the playstyle single source ⟦1⟧.

50dac8b9.en: Investing Stigma Shards evenly across many Stigmas instead of maxing the two or three actually equipped first, diluting overall power ⟦1⟧.

84a07cc3.en: The two or three actually equipped are Assault Stance and Zikel's Blessing.

cf8dc927.en: Inferred from the general Stigma spend-priority advice, applied to the Gladiator-specific picks documented above.

9bf00cb7.en: Gladiator info leans on KR-era community guides; gear-name localization and reset timing remain unconfirmed.

d1becb2e.en: The exact recommended armor, accessory, and weapon set names could not be fully verified against global localization; flagged as single-source with a translation-accuracy caveat rather than fully unverifiable.
