fbe0a4cd.en: Role: Melee DPS. Difficulty: Hard. Weapon: Dual Dagger (sword or bow noted as secondary/off options by some guides).

5390b093.en: Assassin is a hard, high-ceiling melee striker: stealth in, burst from behind, then disengage.

02ab6042.en: The Assassin is a melee DPS class wielding daggers, with dual-dagger as the core setup and sword or bow noted as secondary/off options by some guides ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

afccdce3.en: It plays as a hit-and-run striker:

714d8d79.en: Unload a fast dagger combo, Quick Slice and Flash Slice, for back-attack burst.

c0afb9ee.en: Disengage or weave defensively with Evasion Stance.

248b4cd1.en: This phrasing appears near-verbatim across sources (confirmed) ⟦1⟧.

d6679c0e.en: Rated Hard by at least one general beginner guide, which calls Assassin "suited for experienced players who enjoy positioning" and "not recommended for new players due to their high skill floor" ⟦1⟧.

7e950e58.en: A separate class-explainer source calls Assassin the class with the highest skill ceiling and an active melee combo game ⟦1⟧.

2a067670.en: Confirmed by two independent sources that this is not a beginner-friendly class, so expect a learning curve around positioning and animation-canceling.

b1e474f5.en: Considered the best PvE class for clearing content per early focus-group-test (FGT) player rankings, ahead of Ranger ⟦1⟧

e5be3076.en: Gains more from a short PvP engagement than from standing on a boss for an extended damage test, implying weaker sustained PvE parse damage relative to ranged casters ⟦1⟧

5ba14c7d.en: Treat Assassin as strong-to-top PvE burst but not the most forgiving sustained-DPS pick.

e4161ec2.en: Multiple sources describe Assassin as a top-tier PvP class.

68f3ddaa.en: "Was the KR launch problem child, too strong. Nerfs brought it back to earth. It's still top-tier PvP, just no longer unfair." kr-era ⟦1⟧

56a018ac.en: Strengths: heavy burst, stealth engages, gap closers. Weaknesses: unforgiving punishment for bad openers, real melee risk.

955f0b79.en: A Season 2 balance pass reportedly buffed Assassin further for both PvE and PvP, improving its standing in new endgame dungeons and the Abyss (same source, KR-era, subject to change before global launch)

11734393.en: Party demand: Assassin falls under "damage" roles rather than the guaranteed party-demand roles held by Templar/Cleric/Chanter-type support and tank classes. It is wanted for burst but is not an auto-invite the way support classes are ⟦1⟧.

178975c8.en: Who should pick it: players who enjoy tight positioning, animation-cancel timing, and a high-risk/high-reward melee duelist playstyle, and who accept a rougher early learning curve for a strong PvP ceiling and competitive-to-top PvE burst.

6593bb51.en: Bring Quick Slice, Heart Gore, Insignia Explosion, and Savage Roar to level 20 first.

7b99138e.en: Early leveling priority (single source, detailed): Quick Slash, Roar of the Beast, Ambush, Surprise Attack, and Pattern Explosion are named as the foundational early kit, with emphasis on mastering normal-attack canceling, left-click a normal attack then right-click a skill quickly to remove animation delay ⟦1⟧ kr-era.

ab303f6d.en: Bring to level 20 first: Quick Slice, Heart Gore, Insignia Explosion, Savage Roar ⟦1⟧

09ad8d8e.en: Secondary/flex skills: Storm Rampage (lvl 16), Shadow Fall (lvl 12+), Whirlwind Slice (lvl 12/16), Flash Slice (lvl 8+), Infiltrate (lvl 8+), Defiance (lvl 12/16) ⟦1⟧

f0ed1044.en: Passive priority order: Rear Smite, then Assault Stance, then Exploit Weakness, then Impact Hit (confirmed, two independent extractions of the same source agree)

d925a731.en: Avoid: spreading Skill Points across all abilities instead of committing to the core breakpoint skills; this is called out as a known beginner mistake ⟦1⟧.

31eb2265.en: Mastery/chain skills: Assassin uses a "chain system" where skills connect into one another to extend combos for higher DPS or utility such as pulls, stuns, and lifesteal via chained follow-ups ⟦1⟧ (single source, could not verify by direct fetch, 403).

26976057.en: Pattern Explosion into Heart Gore/Heart Stab, argued as better before your mastery investment is finished ⟦1⟧ kr-era

1a7c08c3.en: Heart Gore/Heart Stab into Pattern Explosion, argued as better once mastery investment is finished (same KR thread, contested ordering) kr-era

c253ecd3.en: Skill names vary by translation: "Heart Gore," "Heart Stab," and "Heart" (as in "Heart normal-attack cancel") likely refer to the same or a closely related skill across scraped guides. Flagged as contested naming rather than confirmed identical.

38b7d008.en: Push Heart Pierce and Pattern Explosion to skill Lv 16 first, then lock in Triniel's Dagger as your first stigma.

1335a30a.en: This order comes from Korean Inven Assassin board consensus across several live-server posts, cross-checked against an English fan site that instead targets skill Lv 20 ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧. Every target below is the skill's own level, its 8/12/16/20 breakpoints, not your character level, since no source ties a step to one.

f104ba9e.en: crit resets cooldown, restores mental force

515a5673.en: Matches the Skill Point budget an actual leveling character has ⟦1⟧

e3265d3c.en: Core four, Quick Slice, Heart Gore, Insignia Explosion, Savage Roar, to 20 before any stagger, recovery, or movement skill ⟦1⟧

404263fa.en: Then Storm Rampage to 16, Shadow Fall to 12+, Whirlwind Slice/Defiance to 12/16, Flash Slice/Infiltrate to 8+ ⟦1⟧

6ec65f8d.en: For pure leveling, follow the KR consensus. Skill Lv 20 needs Daevanion plus Arcana investment that only becomes realistic post-45, so treat the Field Manual's core-four-to-20 order as an endgame target, not a leveling goal ⟦1⟧.

47c2ee60.en: First: Rear Smite, also named Backstab in the Korean order below, very likely the same passive under different translations ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

aa1bd577.en: Then, English order: Assault Stance, Exploit Weakness, Impact Hit, see Skill priority above ⟦1⟧

569948b2.en: Korean order instead: Defense Crack, Exploit Opening, unreconciled with the English list ⟦1⟧

44469609.en: Push the lifesteal chain, animation-cancel from the start

e41c8c8f.en: A weak early investment in Quick Strike makes leveling feel clunky, see Rotation and combos below for the opener ⟦1⟧.

daca6063.en: Daevanion opens, two cooldown nodes first on Nezekan

fdd1f4c3.en: Then cheap attack/crit tiles toward the orange node; by around Lv 20 you should fund two core nodes each on Nezekan and Zikel ⟦1⟧.

7b2ed5d0.en: Stigma unlocks, two orders disagree on the first pick

f14c4a75.en: Illusive Clone first, then Triniel's Dagger ⟦1⟧, or Beast Fangs first per a separate six-slot list ⟦2⟧.

a4cb8c11.en: Both orders still agree Triniel's Dagger and Illusive/Shadow Clone belong in the first few picks, see the note below

df6b5f35.en: Main story and orange quests are the primary leveling path

d608c26f.en: Keep the beginner PvE weave from Rotation and combos running as points and shards fill in around it ⟦1⟧.

8802606d.en: Shift to farming Daevanion and Lord-trace points

449d3cf0.en: Weekly loop of Wanted Order quests, Abyss accessories, expedition gear, and Transcendence Arcana ⟦1⟧.

eacbb71d.en: Hand-off: grow into the skill Lv 20 core four

13a4b4c7.en: See Skill priority above, and Stigma picks and Daevanion board route below, for the full endgame spread.

65b93b94.en: No separate "Leave at level 1" or "Gear while leveling" block: no source names a skill to leave at 1, and the gear enhancement order is the one under Gear and stat priority below.

8abffe47.en: Daevanion unlock level is contested: the class note gives Nezekan at character Lv 12, but a search-aggregated summary of a separate Inven post instead says Nezekan at Lv 10 and Zikel at Lv 20, lower-confidence since the direct fetch failed ⟦1⟧. Stigma fill order is likewise contested, Illusive Clone first versus Beast Fangs first, though both agree Triniel's Dagger and Illusive/Shadow Clone belong early ⟦2⟧; a live player thread shows this exact trade-off in practice, asking whether to lower Swift Contract to fund Triniel's Dagger, with no visible resolution ⟦3⟧.

bf4ba280.en: First core set at unlock and shortly after

6526da98.en: Illusive Clone, Swift Contract, Triniel's Dagger, and Savage Fang form the core stigma kit.

3b803470.en: The most consistently recommended kit keeps major cooldowns together, gives room for defensive play, and performs well without a perfect run, with Evasion Stance as a common defensive pick for the flexible slot ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

0588a153.en: Swift Contract (also seen as "Contract of Swiftness")

68cd1de5.en: Confirmed across 2+ independent sources for the core four.

72e8ee05.en: Triniel's Dagger is repeatedly called the cornerstone stigma, reducing overall skill cooldown at level 10, or roughly 10% recast reduction on hit per one phrasing ⟦1⟧ kr-era ⟦2⟧.

d850e8fc.en: Illusive Clone is separately named as the stigma with the single biggest damage impact, top priority for Stigma Shard investment ⟦1⟧.

22ff4a8a.en: Also called "Phantom Clone" in one search summary.

e2de8042.en: Naming is inconsistent between "Illusive Clone," "Illusion Clone," and "Phantom Clone" across scraped guides, contested naming, likely the same skill.

64015e78.en: Beast's Fang: reduces boss groggy gauge, useful for PvE boss fights

d08f4276.en: Dark Throw: reduces enemy movement speed, PvP utility

64e6cfc6.en: Throw Shadowblade: ranged damage option for the flex slot

73b1e7b0.en: PvE vs PvP: one source explicitly separates the two, noting PvE stigma priority favors mana recovery, lifesteal, and cooldown reduction for rune-detonation skills to sustain damage through longer fights, while PvP favors stealth uptime and stun-duration extension for control ⟦1⟧.

3340ecd6.en: Spend Stigma Shards first on: Illusive/Phantom Clone (highest damage impact per source), then Triniel's Dagger to lock in the cooldown-reduction backbone. Single-source ordering, but the two skills are consistently paired across guides.

7f209d83.en: Boards unlock through level 45; sources disagree whether there are 6 or 8 total.

c68a80f2.en: The Daevanion board unlocks progressively by level.

3ab78e47.en: One wiki source lists six boards: Nezekan (Lv 12), Zikel (Lv 20), Vaizel (Lv 30), Triniel (Lv 40), Ariel (Lv 45), Azphel (Lv 45) ⟦1⟧

f0119904.en: A separate search summary additionally names Marchutan and Yustiel as advanced level-45 boards, for eight total ⟦1⟧

801ac2eb.en: Sources disagree on whether there are 6 or 8 total boards, possibly a page update or a KR/TW-versus-global difference.

117c3e99.en: Node types: grey nodes are stat increases (lowest point cost), green nodes level up passive skills, blue nodes level up active skills, and orange/unique nodes grant special effects (highest point cost) ⟦1⟧. This matches the blue-active/green-passive framing used elsewhere in this guide (confirmed).

d6221877.en: Recommended route: prioritize hitting skill-level breakpoints (12/16/20) over the cheapest tile; ignore point-cost order when a lower-rarity tile completes a breakpoint ⟦1⟧ (single source).

690caa12.en: Attack, then Critical Hit/Accuracy, then HP, then Defense (single source).

879227dc.en: Daevanion Points are earned through general progression and account/character milestones. No AION 2-specific source gave a precise farming list beyond "you will eventually get enough Daevanion Points to cover the entirety of the boards" ⟦1⟧.

13011f5e.en: Post-45 progression involves collecting Lord-trace skill points and farming Daevanion points from sealed/endgame content ⟦1⟧ (single source).

25c209fa.en: kr-era, single source, flagged by the source itself as provisional The only concrete reset cost figure found is a cross-class one, not confirmed Assassin-specific: a Korean patch reportedly set individual Daevanion node resets to 500 Kinah, with the client also supporting a full board reset.

df61c485.en: A dependency rule applies: a node cannot be removed if another already-acquired node depends on it. The source explicitly warns the number could change for global ⟦1⟧.

02e63bfd.en: When to reset, and whether 500 Kinah is Assassin-specific: no reliable source found. A Korean search on "살성 데바니온 초기화 비용" (Assassin Daevanion reset cost) turns up only general discussion of counting activated nodes to estimate total Daevanion Crystal needs before a reset, with no Assassin-specific cost figure contested/unclear ⟦1⟧. Net: reset cost is likely the same 500 Kinah per node cross-class figure, but no second source confirms it is Assassin-specific or unchanged, treat as unconfirmed for Assassin specifically.

b90c39a0.en: No independently confirmed Assassin Arcana mapping; a Scroll/Compass/Chalice/Scales order is documented.

dad7efd9.en: Arcana cards are equipped in card slots to gain Combat Power, passive/active skill bonuses, skill-level "transcendence" past normal caps, set effects, and stat amplification ⟦1⟧ kr-era ⟦2⟧.

511a0448.en: To push a skill to level 20: Daevanion (4) plus Arcana (4) equals 18, with the remaining 2 points from ring slots that can each carry one active-skill line ⟦1⟧ (single source, unverified independently).

9a74cc20.en: A suggested high-end upgrade order, current through 2026-08-12 per the site itself ⟦1⟧:

128d7075.en: Scroll: main active-skill trio (Quick Slice, Heart Gore, Insignia Explosion) in a 4/2 or 3/3/2 level split

8214a86d.en: Compass: secondary actives Savage Roar, Storm Rampage, and Defiance

495d999a.en: Chalice / Scales: pushes passive skill levels (Rear Smite, Assault Stance, Exploit Weakness)

c1e767dc.en: Key/Hourglass slot: offense favors Weapon Damage; Hourglass is "acceptable with PvE resistance"

1f880bae.en: Gap remains, single source confirmed: no independent confirmation of this card-to-skill mapping exists; other sources surface only generic, non-Assassin-specific Arcana explainers covering card types and general Frenzy/Purity/Libra combos, with no independently-authored Assassin-specific card mapping found still single source ⟦1⟧. Treat these exact card-to-skill assignments with caution until a second source turns up.

29e1c9e9.en: What to avoid: no reliable source explicitly listed Arcana cards or configurations Assassin should avoid. General Arcana guides mention that older "meta" configurations (4 Vitality/1 Magic) have been superseded by newer mixes (3 Vitality/2 Magic or 2 Vitality/3 Magic), but this was not tied specifically to Assassin ⟦1⟧ kr-era.

c3594926.en: Stack Critical Hit, Attack, and Accuracy/Penetration; enhance the weapon slot first.

4d4b7ca4.en: Weapon: Dagger (dual-wield is the core identity). One PvP-focused source suggests a Sword (Main) plus Dagger (Off) combination specifically for PvP burst and stun-duration extension ⟦1⟧ (single source, unverified by direct fetch).

2fa0a39e.en: Top stats: Critical Hit, Attack (or Attack Speed), Accuracy/Penetration ⟦1⟧

68d20c0e.en: Secondary: Evasion, as a defensive stat named by one source

98711dc5.en: Example PvE Crit-DPS build: a sample high-crit gear loadout ⟦1⟧

b9a8da1e.en: From a community build using an Archon Praetorian Captain Dagger (+20 enchant, +5 exceed) and a full Splendent Nemesis Dragon Lord armor set. Treat as an example, not a universal target.

01cf0526.en: A separate fan-made source gives this order ⟦1⟧ (single source):

d88d5acb.en: Weapon first: Combat Speed, Might, then Weapon Damage Boost, then Damage Boost

80e5b0a6.en: Pants: Damage Tolerance plus Attack Increase

a13c66e3.en: Jewelry: Attack first, Critical Hit once an accuracy hit-check threshold is met

75078ee7.en: The same source gives a manastone-equivalent order: Back Attack Boost, then Weapon Damage Boost, then Critical Damage Boost, then Attack +25/+30, then Damage Boost.

6db5e426.en: Which piece to enhance first: the weapon, per the Field Manual source above (single source), consistent with general MMO practice of prioritizing main-hand weapon enchant/enhance for DPS classes.

cf04741f.en: Set effects: "Splendent Nemesis Dragon Lord" appears as a named armor set in the example PvE build, described only by its stat contributions rather than an explicit set-bonus description ⟦1⟧ (single source).

9d613f8b.en: Open from stealth with Ambush, weave normal-attack cancels, and finish with Pattern Explosion.

8237d38a.en: Open with Ambush, normal-attack-cancel, Surprise Attack, normal-attack-cancel, Heart (Gore/Stab), normal-attack-cancel, Pattern Explosion, repeating the animation-cancel weave throughout kr-era ⟦1⟧.

2d2cd6ed.en: A separate source frames the loop as maintain rune stacks, detonate with Pattern Explosion at max stacks, weave Quick Slash for mana sustain ⟦1⟧.

40eb7c1b.en: Pop Illusive Clone, Swift Contract, and Savage Fang together ⟦1⟧ (single source)

d04ddd8e.en: Run your four core rear-positioned attacks during the resulting buff window

f32acf32.en: If Illusive Clone is on cooldown, deploy Storm Rampage during a boss's stagger/groggy window instead

2f34ffe7.en: Buff timing: hold Triniel's Dagger for only 3-8 seconds to keep buff alignment tight (single source).

fc213251.en: Stealth only right before engaging, to avoid wasting duration. Open with Ambush from behind for the maximum damage multiplier, chain into Surprise Attack, and finish with Pattern Explosion ⟦1⟧ (single source).

08f90db5.en: A separate PvP combo listing gives: Illusion Clone buff, Ambush, Shadow Fall, Wide Slash, Triniel's Dagger plus Ambush kr-era ⟦1⟧.

5c8e8617.en: Defensive/utility cooldowns: Evasion Stance and Shadow Walk (a stealth-based defensive/repositioning tool) are named as the class's core defensive kit, used to avoid downtime during rotation rather than only reactively ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

737aad73.en: Auto-hunt/macro setup: a Korean-language thread describes a basic key-binding scheme for leveling, Q for movement/gap-close skills (Assassination, Flash Slash, Penetration-type skills), E for core damage skills (Heart-piercing, Ambush, Whirlwind Slash), R for conditional/finisher effects (Pattern Explosion), plus Spacebar to help reset the cycle ⟦1⟧ kr-era. Single source, informal community post, treat as illustrative rather than authoritative.

599e56c6.en: Assassin levels well once breakpoint skills land around level 20, but needs careful positioning.

e9689e1a.en: Solo leveling comfort: sources agree Assassin can level efficiently once its early breakpoint skills (level 16/20 traits) are secured, but is not considered the most beginner-forgiving class due to its reliance on positioning ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

c9ef997e.en: Sustain: PvE-focused guides recommend prioritizing mana recovery and lifesteal-adjacent stigma/skill options during leveling to reduce downtime between pulls ⟦1⟧.

3ecaf65e.en: One fan-made source splits leveling into two phases:

d07e820b.en: Before level 45: follow main story and orange quest objectives

b555913a.en: After level 45: shift to collecting Lord-trace skill points and farming Daevanion points from sealed/endgame content ⟦1⟧ (single source)

71e524fa.en: Weekly loop: Wanted Order quests, Abyss accessories, expedition gear, and Transcendence Arcana.

d49dabc3.en: When the class "turns on": no source gave an exact level, but the recurring theme across guides is that Assassin's core identity (rear-attack multipliers, Illusive Clone plus Triniel's Dagger buff-chaining) only comes online once its level-20-ish core skills and matching stigmas are unlocked, implying a slower start than simpler classes. Synthesized from multiple sources above, not a direct quote.

67cf41e1.en: Time stealth right before engaging, always attack from behind, and swap builds for PvE vs PvP.

6ed8f20c.en: Poor stealth timing, entering stealth too early wastes its duration; it should be used right before the opening attack ⟦1⟧.

51bfb3d2.en: Ignoring positioning, most of the class's damage multipliers require back attacks, so failing to reposition constantly caps your DPS ⟦1⟧.

b90061f8.en: Misusing rune/insignia stacking, detonating stacks with Pattern Explosion at the wrong stack count instead of at full stacks is called out as a major DPS loss ⟦1⟧.

ae858d94.en: Using the same build/stigma setup for both PvE and PvP instead of swapping loadouts ⟦1⟧.

eb0d5707.en: Spreading Skill Points evenly across all abilities instead of committing to level 16/20 breakpoint skills first ⟦1⟧.

3bc7d6c9.en: Over-investing in gear that will be replaced almost immediately, instead of pacing enhancement spend to milestone gear ⟦1⟧ (could not verify by direct fetch, 403, single source).

5f37b444.en: Chasing a "perfect" meta build in the first 40 levels instead of just leveling with the core kit ⟦1⟧.

b8827f85.en: Holding Triniel's Dagger too long, breaking buff-window alignment with your core attack chain, instead of using it in the recommended 3-8 second window ⟦1⟧ (single source).

5a451fd3.en: Letting Illusive Clone/Swift Contract cooldowns drift out of sync instead of chaining them together at the start of a damage window ⟦1⟧ (single source).

321aa7c7.en: Dropping defensive tools (Evasion Stance) too early in a fight, leaving no answer for incoming burst since Assassin has low innate durability, "fragility and short reach" per the class overview ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

4e4b1a1d.en: Assassin info leans on one fan-made field manual plus KR-era community threads and boosting-site guides.

e1a8c90e.en: Role: Ranged magic DPS. Difficulty: Very high (S-tier). Weapon: Spellbook.

8dcdb168.en: DPSRangedMagicGlass cannonNot beginner friendly

4a93d85a.en: Sourcing note: AION 2 launched in KR/TW in November 2025 and is pre-launch for the October 5, 2026 global release. Most guides below are KR/TW-era. Skill and Stigma names are fan translations of Korean text, not confirmed global localization strings, so treat exact English names as approximate.

536ec2a3.en: Sorcerer is a glass-cannon ranged mage: huge burst and AoE, very low HP, and the steepest learning curve in the game.

2b6f19e3.en: Ranged magic damage dealer wielding a Spellbook, built around fire and ice magic ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

f6bd24c9.en: Consistently described as a "glass cannon nuker": very high burst and AoE damage combined with very low HP and defense ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

c6b1aa27.en: Difficulty is rated at the top of the roster. One difficulty-focused tier list places Sorcerer in S-tier (hardest), right beside Assassin, citing extremely low survivability, unforgiving positioning requirements, and a high skill ceiling with almost no forgiveness for mistakes single source ⟦1⟧.

310d14af.en: contested PvE vs PvP ranking

c8847854.en: PvE grade: A, "with a real claim on higher"

cf72c286.en: PvP grade: B, limited by survivability in extended trades

c87f756f.en: PvE grade: C-tier, only 83 of 800 tracked leaderboard slots

8b063a66.en: Argues the class "wants to stand still and cast" while harder encounters demand movement

3d811cd7.en: These two rankings genuinely disagree. aion2boost.com is a marketing/boosting site grading on theoretical ceiling; allthings.how claims to use actual leaderboard participation data. Both are pre-launch, single-source assessments, treat the true PvE standing as unsettled until global launch data exists.

7e48a4c6.en: Party demand: Sorcerer is generally cited as a top-tier AoE and single-target burst DPS with strong CC utility for parties, but its fragility means it depends heavily on positioning support and boss mechanic knowledge ⟦1⟧.

69c43028.en: Who should pick it: players who enjoy planning burst windows, are comfortable with high-risk, high-reward positioning, and are willing to relearn spell timing rather than face-tank mistakes.

29ec40f8.en: Not for beginners: Sorcerer is not a "forgiving" first class. Spiritmaster or a melee class is an easier on-ramp by comparison.

d43f5637.en: No confirmed global skill order exists yet; two KR-era guides disagree, so treat exact names and levels as provisional.

d48359e3.en: Tier 2 (level 12): "Icy Wind" (CC/grouping) and "Flame Arrow" (basic attack, mana/fire-mark spec)

02b8a95c.en: Invest skill points to reach level 16 on core skills before spending on stat gear

503b7537.en: From the SlashingCreeps source: Priority 1 = "Fire mark," "Evaporation," "Thanks to the improvement" (likely mistranslated names); Priority 2 = "Earth's Robe," "Contract," "Grace of the Resistance," "Flame Robe"; Priority 3 = defensive/resistance passives single source, low confidence in names ⟦1⟧.

70062538.en: Confirmed, higher-confidence names across wiki-style sources (not tied to a specific leveling order): Firebomb, Firestorm, Blaze, Ice Chain, Cold Snap ⟦1⟧.

8fc5a0e5.en: A separate translated list, explicitly marked as from an in-progress, pre-launch build subject to change, names Cool Down, Fire Spell, Hellfire, Ice Break, and The Wisdom of Lumiere as core kit pieces kr-era ⟦1⟧.

9d7ecc58.en: Ice Break resets Cool Down on crit and Cool Down can reset Glacier Strike's cooldown, suggesting a freeze-into-burst chain design.

4ca89ea2.en: Translation conflict: "Firestorm/Hellfire" (SlashingCreeps, aion2hub) and "Fire Spell/Hellfire" (Fextralife) likely describe overlapping Korean skills under different fan translations. Treat exact spelling as unconfirmed pending global localization.

777102dc.en: A separate KR-focused Arcana guide gives its own concrete priority, using KR terms translated as "Flaming Arrow" and "Flaming Burst": level 불꽃 화살 (Flaming Arrow) to 20 first as the primary target, with 불꽃 폭발 (Flaming Burst) to 20 as the secondary option kr-era single source ⟦1⟧.

9d7bcd44.en: Players who struggle with Flaming Arrow's accuracy or hit requirements are advised to use 호한의 바람 (Wind of Regret) plus Flaming Burst instead, both leveled to 20.

6f27edfc.en: Gap remains: no reliable source gives a definitive "level this first" active skill order using confirmed global skill names, or mastery/chain-skill specifics (which skill upgrades unlock chain follow-ups). The KR-language order above is the most concrete leveling priority currently available, but it uses KR terms translated by a single guide, not confirmed global names. Closest cross-guide agreement: reach level 16 on your core damage skill before investing in stat gear, per u4n.com above.

a1f84334.en: No official AION 2 global skill-name glossary has been published pre-launch. The only officially confirmed global information is the roster of 8 launch classes and a Launch Scale Test running September 17-18, 2026; no skill-by-skill or stigma-by-stigma English naming had been published as of 2026-09-12. Every English skill name used in this card, and elsewhere in this guide, is an unofficial fan translation ⟦1⟧.

416dd141.en: Push Flame Arrow and Ice Chain to 7, then Flame Spear and Flame Burst to 7, all four to 10, then Hellfire; open Stigmas with Delayed Explosion.

9e8aa0f2.en: This order comes from Korean community threads and guide sites (Inven and a Korean blog aggregator) that independently converge on the same early sequence. Every step is the skill's own level, capped at 10 by Skill Points, not your character level, unless a step says otherwise.

efccf08a.en: the basic-attack chain, core of the early kit

5c278938.en: core damage pair, life-steal plus a delayed hit

f27eedf8.en: a Daevanion point cheapens the Lv 7 to 8 step first

073b807f.en: adds AoE and CC once the core four are set

ac754e3c.en: main burst finisher, cooldown cut by Flame Spear

0af7a20b.en: No skill to leave untouched at level 1 turned up in the research; every skill named above gets points as soon as it is available.

fa994b8f.en: Keep Ice Chain and Howling Wind in the core rotation alongside the Fire skills through the order above ⟦1⟧

ce201b8a.en: A live leveling thread runs a genuinely Ice-invested Daevanion path early and only plans a Fire pivot once better geared ⟦1⟧

3430051c.en: One guide cores the kit on five Fire skills only, Flame Arrow, Flame Burst, Hellfire, Flame Snare, and Origin of Focus, each to skill Lv 20, and says to abandon the Ice skill Freezing Explosion ⟦1⟧

6ec0df4f.en: A separate Arcana guide instead ranks Flame Arrow, then Flame Burst, then Flame Spear to skill Lv 20, keeping Howling Wind only as a fallback ⟦1⟧

a50ba5ac.en: Follow Variant A while leveling: a live thread confirms players run a genuinely Ice-invested Daevanion route early ⟦1⟧, then pivot toward Variant B's pure-Fire cooldown chain once gear and Daevanion points allow it.

b7d3cec4.en: First: Flame Robe (불꽃의 로브 / 대지의 로브, contested naming), top PvE passive per this guide ⟦1⟧

cadb99de.en: Later: Life Evaporation (생기 증발), then Frost/Chill Summon for its bonus damage against Ice Chain's slow ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

80530006.en: A separate source orders passives as Grace Enhancement, then Earth Robe, then Chill Summon instead, a contested reshuffle of the same short list ⟦1⟧

4a866ce8.en: Run the order above: both basics to 7, then the Fire damage pair to 7

416664e6.en: Weave Flame Spear and Flame Burst into the Flame Arrow/Ice Chain basic-attack chain rather than casting them stand-alone ⟦1⟧

1000899d.en: Grab two cheap cooldown-reduction nodes first, then 1-point attack nodes over attack-speed nodes, pushing the core three skills past Lv 12 ⟦1⟧

9918a54c.en: Two sources put Delayed Explosion (지연 폭발) at the top of the Stigma build, ahead of Divine Explosion, Steel Protection, and Chill Storm ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

5fb355f3.en: Keep the hybrid rotation and a life-steal gear setup while gear is thin

8fee5142.en: Sources describe this stretch as the point to still be running Variant A, ice-invested and stable, rather than forcing an early Fire pivot ⟦1⟧

671cb5ea.en: Pivot toward Variant B's pure-Fire cooldown chain once geared

8c06b62d.en: See the Skill priority, Stigma picks, and Daevanion board route cards above and below for the endgame spread this leveling order feeds into.

23890dc7.en: Run a life-steal-oriented setup for stable, low-risk clearing, then switch itemization toward burst once a Winter's Binding-centered rotation is viable ⟦1⟧

1ef3cb82.en: The Fire/Ice split above is a genuine disagreement, not just translation noise: one live leveling thread runs Ice-invested through the leveling stretch ⟦1⟧, while a separate guide recommends abandoning Ice investment for a pure-Fire core ⟦2⟧

df03e46d.en: Avoid: chasing burst rotations before your gear supports them; lean on the basic-attack chain and a life-steal setup while leveling ⟦1⟧

1e720e87.en: Stigmas unlock at 23 with 5 slots; prioritize damage amplification for PvE and escape tools for PvP.

ff26d648.en: Stigmas unlock at level 23 ⟦1⟧. As of the March 25, 2026 KR patch the maximum equippable Stigma slots was expanded to 5, and Mastery/Stigma skills can now share slots kr-era ⟦2⟧.

27c7705f.en: Advanced Stigma content (a Korean guidebook) also expanded the level cap from 20 to 25 with a higher-tier Stigma Shard for content above level 20; global launch cap for this system is not yet confirmed ⟦1⟧.

03f6f57c.en: The same March 25, 2026 patch added a brand-new Sorcerer-specific Stigma called "Hibernation," alongside buffs making "Lumiel's Space" into an AoE skill and a +20% damage increase to "Hellfire" kr-era, balance may change ⟦1⟧.

b7fda20e.en: A lower-trust build guide lists early Stigma tiers as: Tier 1 = "Steel barrier" (a shield) and "Improvement of elements"; Tier 2 = "Divine Explosion" and "Firewall" single source, low trust ⟦1⟧.

2a95fd8f.en: Area pages deepen the multi-target engine and mana economy

5b08cdcb.en: PvP pages spend real slots on escape tools and anti-melee defense rather than pure damage

ef50c4bb.en: PvE Stigma priority: damage amplification first, control second, survivability third. PvP priority: escape/anti-melee first, control second, burst third ⟦1⟧.

401dcec3.en: A Sorcerer-specific PvE Stigma investment order was also found: 원소강화 (Elemental Enhancement) first, 불의장벽 (Fire Wall) second, 지연폭발 (Delayed Explosion) third, then 강철보호막 (Steel Shield) fourth kr-era single source (exact source URL not individually isolated from a multi-result search synthesis, treat as an unconfirmed community claim, date unknown).

092ca381.en: Gap remains: no reliable source found for a specific recommended Stigma loadout naming exact global skill IDs, or for what to spend Stigma Shards on first beyond the general "fund frequently-used Stigmas" progression order ⟦1⟧.

5a9bf602.en: Shared cross-class board unlocking at 12; prioritize blue active-skill nodes early, with ice-vs-fire routing differing by spec.

d4679ab2.en: The Daevanion board is a shared system across all classes, not Sorcerer-specific, but the mechanics matter for build planning. It unlocks at level 12 ⟦1⟧.

5b8411e8.en: Node types and costs: grey = stat nodes (1 Daevanion Point), green = passive skill level-ups (2 points), blue = active skill level-ups (3 points), orange = unique specialty nodes at the board periphery granting bonuses like cooldown reduction or critical damage (4 points) ⟦1⟧.

7cc62efc.en: Ariel is PvE Damage/Tolerance, Azphel is PvP Damage/Tolerance. Two more advanced boards, Marchutan and Yustiel, are referenced elsewhere as also unlocking at 45 single source for naming.

78c75c40.en: Recommended early route (general, not Sorcerer-specific): prioritize blue (active skill) nodes early to maximize immediate combat power, since nodes must be unlocked sequentially outward from the board's center and route choice matters as much as the final destination.

5df41258.en: aion2boost.com's Sorcerer-specific framing: for PvE, invest cooldown reduction and skill-potency nodes; area-focused players should lean into multi-target support nodes, single-target/burst players into burst-alignment nodes marketing source ⟦1⟧.

8b98e55c.en: Reset mechanics: Korean live service currently offers free resets for Mastery Skills and Stigmas; Daevanion individual-node resets cost 500 Kinah on KR live, but global costs are unconfirmed kr-era ⟦1⟧.

19c28985.en: A KR community source adds general (not node-specific) routing guidance: prioritize skill-level and corner (bonus) nodes first, then required passives, then remaining attack-stat options kr-era single source ⟦1⟧.

92d1a629.en: Early routing reportedly differs depending on whether a Sorcerer specializes into ice or fire, since the split is core to the class's kit, with community threads discussing a separate "early ice Daevanion tree" build.

578054ef.en: Gap remains: no Sorcerer-specific node-by-node Daevanion route (exact nodes in order) has been found. Closest available guidance is the general "prioritize blue nodes early" advice, aion2boost's PvE framing above, and the ice-vs-fire specialization routing note just above.

e4f460ed.en: Fill Arcana slots immediately with usable cards rather than waiting for perfect drops, then focus Training Arcana on keepers.

94490bdd.en: Arcana is a shared cross-class system. Current KR/TW Arcana slot types include the original five (Chalice, Parchment, Compass, Bell, Mirror) plus Scales, Key, Hourglass, Dice, and Lantern kr-era, balance may change ⟦1⟧.

6ef097f7.en: Cards come in Common, Rare, Epic, and Unique grades; general advice is to fill empty slots immediately with usable lower-grade cards rather than waiting for perfect drops, since even a lower-grade card provides item level, stats, set progress, and skill levels.

2b5b53a6.en: Leveling Arcana uses Training Arcana consumables (KR/TW values: Lesser 200 EXP, Intermediate 600, Superior 1,500, Ultimate 3,000); use Training Arcana only on cards you intend to keep rather than spreading it across filler cards.

f52b0054.en: For DPS classes generally, Sorcerer included, the guidance is to prioritize cards that increase levels on the active skills and passives driving your main rotation, then complete damage-oriented set bonuses ⟦1⟧.

b6430d29.en: Check individual skill breakpoints, particularly around skill levels 16 to 20, rather than assume a universal formula.

ac55a746.en: Avoid: spreading Training Arcana across cards you do not plan to keep.

b3d9d6bc.en: Chalice and Parchment: prioritize Flaming Burst and Flaming Arrow stats

1d97685c.en: Compass: Wind of Regret (호한의 바람), explicitly not Flame Barrage

562867d3.en: Bell: Mark of Flame, Cold Summoning, and Contract of Rebirth

72a58d67.en: Mirror: Fiery Robes, Life Drain, and Spirit Absorption

007af70e.en: These English names are informal translations of KR terms from a single guide and are not confirmed official localizations kr-era single source, fan-translated names ⟦1⟧.

51b0ae94.en: This slotting order is single-source and KR-era, not independently corroborated. Treat exact card and skill names as provisional until a second source or global localization confirms them.

ce0131e5.en: Spellbook and cloth armor are fixed; put Intelligence and Magic Attack first, then Cooldown Reduction.

bd544ff8.en: Weapon: Spellbook (confirmed across all sources). Armor type: cloth, standard for the class ⟦1⟧.

3796ee41.en: Two build paths recur across sources (confirmed pattern, single source on the exact stat lists):

2a6049ae.en: Prioritizes Critical Hit, Accuracy, and Attack% for maximum single-target/AoE burst

4cb4b099.en: One source names "White Dragon Lord Tome" as a recommended weapon single source, unverifiable

ff573499.en: Prioritizes crowd control uptime and mobility

c649e6c6.en: Aimed at PvP and solo challenging PvE

b16e224b.en: Do first: Intelligence and Magic Attack as primary offensive stats over physical defense

9c4dba40.en: Then: Cooldown Reduction, called "essential" via Daevanion allocation

aa8d5eb4.en: Later / optional: Critical hits, Accuracy, life stats

78149ae5.en: A separate guide's blunt framing: "aim for the skills to be achieved at level 16 and attack, critical hits and life last," implying skill-level breakpoints matter more early than raw stat itemization ⟦1⟧.

b0ba7cb9.en: Manastone/Godstone-equivalent system (shared, not Sorcerer-specific): gear has 2 to 4 randomly generated sockets; Manastones slot into weapons/armor and Spiritstones into accessories, with sockets often needing to be unlocked via Manastone Fasteners from gear extraction kr-era ⟦1⟧.

c9a0bf47.en: Godstones can be socketed onto enchanted items for extra combat effects and can be reset via "soul imprinting."

489d0b8d.en: One methodology guide explicitly declined to give stat priority, cautioning that "actual skill details require checking the live client" rather than trusting pre-launch numbers ⟦1⟧.

d5981842.en: Cross-class general guidance: weapon first, then the Guard/chest piece and accessories kr-era single source, general not Sorcerer-exclusive ⟦1⟧.

94824d5a.en: Remaining armor pieces (gloves, body, boots) are enhanced steadily for long-term use starting mid-progression.

cd6ce5a0.en: The same source separately flags Daevanion, the Amulet of Revelation, and the Belt of Nobility as the three biggest early item-level gains to prioritize.

03d60b9a.en: Gap remains: no reliable source found naming the specific Manastone/Godstone options a Sorcerer should chase, or confirmed Sorcerer set-effect bonuses. General cross-guide advice: raise core damage-skill levels via gear, Daevanion, and Arcana before chasing pure stat lines.

cfe609ec.en: Freeze with Ice skills, then dump your highest-damage Fire spells into the CC window.

602ec37e.en: The most consistent mechanical description across sources is a freeze-then-burst (Ice into Fire) pattern: use Ice skills to slow, freeze, or root a target so it cannot close distance or escape, then align your highest-damage Fire spells during that CC window ⟦1⟧.

d3bf41ce.en: This is reinforced by the wiki's Cool Down/Ice Break/Hellfire interactions, where Cool Down freezes for 3 seconds and can reset Glacier Strike's cooldown, and Ice Break deals bonus damage to frozen targets while resetting Cool Down on a critical hit, describing a genuine freeze-lock combo loop kr-era, in-progress build ⟦1⟧.

2f6a6c8c.en: Use a defensive shield Stigma proactively

03217ed6.en: Open trash packs with AoE spells for grouping and aggro (one source calls this skill "Glacial Wind" for aggro control)

09966915.en: Transition to single-target burst skills for tougher enemies and bosses

627391b4.en: One Korean-sourced guide, translated names, contested confidence:

1d550f91.en: Bind priority skills (translated "Soothing Wind," "Winter's Rest," "Hellfire," "Concentration") to a shared macro key

a652ee40.en: Use manually-controlled skills first (translated "Elemental Reinforcement," "Wall of Fire," "Frost Storm") before triggering the macro

f04c2d37.en: Alternate left/right click basic attacks smoothly to cancel animations

89716ed4.en: Flags that a live balance patch changed right-click Ice Chain attack speed, requiring a skill-speed adjustment kr-era ⟦1⟧

6797bd20.en: Defensive/utility cooldowns: mobility tools (referred to as "Blink" in one source) are used to disengage from melee threats like Assassins ⟦1⟧. "The Wisdom of Lumiere," which halves MP cost of all skills for 10 seconds, is named as a burst-window enabler in the wiki skill list ⟦2⟧.

c72361cd.en: No pet/spirit management applies to Sorcerer, it is not a summoner class.

8f6a080b.en: Pull to your control budget, not your damage; the class turns on once its AoE/CC engine comes online around level 16.

ac8cff78.en: Solo leveling comfort is rated lower than average due to fragility: guides repeatedly stress "pull to your control budget, not your damage" as a core leveling habit, since the packs you can lock down with CC are the packs you can safely clear ⟦1⟧.

4bd35184.en: Sustain is weak; the class has no core self-heal beyond shields and burst kill speed, so early levels require "fragile, methodical play," per aion2boost.com, until the area-damage engine comes online mid-progression for faster pack-clearing.

952d30bb.en: Beginner tip: treat positioning, not a stat, as your primary defensive tool. Avoid pulling beyond your control capacity.

af746789.en: When the class "turns on": sources agree the AoE/CC engine strengthens noticeably in the mid-teens once Firestorm/Hellfire-tier skills and their Daevanion nodes are online, roughly the level-16 gate referenced by multiple guides ⟦1⟧.

913622d5.en: This is corroborated by a layered framework recommending players first lock in safe positioning and cancellation mechanics before layering in damage output.

b6516cdf.en: Most mistakes come from casting without a safe position or an escape plan already picked.

78038b6f.en: Standing still to finish a cast instead of pre-selecting a safe casting position before committing confirmed, multiple sources ⟦1⟧

79213af1.en: Relocating after every single cast instead of preserving movement options for upcoming mechanics ⟦1⟧

e2155bbe.en: Long-committing to a cast before knowing an upcoming boss mechanic or phase transition ⟦1⟧

fa03acda.en: Positioning outside of party support and safe-zone escape routes ⟦1⟧

c1997859.en: Treating all enemy groups as stationary, ignoring gap-closers ⟦1⟧

6ed905a9.en: Pulling more mobs than your CC (control budget) can actually lock down, rather than pulling to your theoretical damage output ⟦1⟧

5622afdd.en: Using outdated coefficient/damage data imported from the original AION rather than verifying live client numbers ⟦1⟧

81b36ac2.en: Treating a training-dummy rotation as "optimal" without accounting for movement interruptions in real fights ⟦1⟧

a5eae647.en: In PvP, spending every defensive cooldown while the opponent is still probing rather than saving them for the real engagement ⟦1⟧

c3c3ef6d.en: Not pre-planning an escape route in PvP before engaging, leading to being caught out as "free kills" ⟦1⟧

b7df2e01.en: Role: Ranged magic DPS (pet class). Difficulty: Moderate, deceptively deep. Weapon: Orb.

1eb82aa4.en: DPSRangedMagicPet classSolo friendly

ab74feea.en: Sourcing note: AION 2 launched KR/TW live in November 2025; global PC launch is October 5, 2026. Most guides below are KR/TW-era. Skill and Stigma names are independent fan translations of Korean text, not confirmed global localization strings, so where two sources give different English names for what appears to be the same skill, both are listed. The class is also called "Elementalist" on some wiki sources, an earlier or alternate translation rather than a separate class.

d10b1cd6.en: Spiritmaster is a pet-based ranged mage: safer and more forgiving than Sorcerer, but its rotation is deeper than it looks.

9fa9a131.en: Ranged magic damage dealer wielding an Orb, built around summoning and rotating four elemental spirits (Fire, Water, Wind, Earth) ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

190dd205.en: Stacks damage-over-time effects, debuffs, and fear-based crowd control from range while the spirits act as semi-autonomous, turret-like damage sources rather than a single persistent pet ⟦1⟧

74e1bf1f.en: Rated notably lower than Sorcerer: a difficulty-focused tier list places Spiritmaster (referred to there as "Spiritmaster/Elementalist") in its most beginner-friendly bracket, citing "more safety tools than Sorcerer" and a more forgiving learning curve while still delivering respectable damage single source ⟦1⟧.

43211308.en: Other guides stress the rotation itself is deceptively demanding: many new players pick it up expecting a simple pet class, then get overwhelmed by the rotation, with the real skill expressed through spirit-cycle management, not simple button-pressing search-summary only, source 403'd ⟦1⟧.

577a2b3b.en: PvE grade: C, "burst is the roster's floor"

9ba0d7a7.en: PvP grade: C, vulnerable to any mechanic that neutralizes summons

d3fba8dc.en: Praises latency tolerance: "summons keep fighting through lag that cripples every reaction-based kit"

10f5bdd4.en: PvE grade: D-tier, the lowest of any class, only 34 of 800 tracked leaderboard slots

6168e299.en: Concludes it "asks the most and returns the least in the current PvE meta"

2be6cdf8.en: Claims Spiritmaster is "the best current PvE DPS recommendation"

6c3698c7.en: Claims an A-tier rating as "the biggest winner of pre-launch balance passes"

a962709c.en: Search-summary only, direct fetch returned HTTP 403, unverified against original text

bbc030fd.en: These three assessments genuinely conflict, from a D-tier "asks the most, returns the least" verdict to an A-tier "biggest winner" claim. Treat Spiritmaster's PvE ranking as unsettled rather than settled.

34eb97a8.en: Its PvP framing is more consistent: sources agree it offers safer, more controlled ranged pressure than melee classes, with strong 1v1 utility from pet pressure plus fear-based crowd control ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

1832b891.en: Party demand: cited as strong for sustained pressure and solo self-sufficiency but more mechanically demanding in group content where boss movement can disrupt spirit positioning ⟦1⟧.

ad1cb1a5.en: Who should pick it: players who want a self-sufficient solo class with built-in "pet tank" survivability and are willing to learn spirit-cycle management rather than a simple rotation. A reasonable beginner-friendly pick relative to Sorcerer, but not a truly "easy" class once the rotation depth is considered.

3b6b0745.en: Both major guides agree Spirit Strike is the top passive; everything else uses different fan-translated names.

929501a3.en: Two independent guides give partially conflicting skill names for what appears to be the same core kit; both are reported here (contested naming, single source each for specific priority order).

33db755b.en: Recommends a "Three Spirit Warala" setup using Fire, Water, and Earth spirits, explicitly stating that adding a fourth, Wind Spirit, "slows down the rotation and lowers overall damage efficiency."

b4848ec6.en: Do first: Cold Shock (lifesteal/survival), Flame Transfer (strong damage), a mobility specialization (called essential)

92313065.en: Then: Ancient Spirit (critical timing-dependent), Elemental Fusion (damage and instant-trigger chance)

14a96bca.en: Later / optional: Fire Spirit as primary summon, Water Spirit secondary, Earth Spirit situational

22ed922b.en: Passive priority: Spirit Strike and Focus (direct damage) first, then Spirit Regeneration (resource recovery for Ancient Spirit).

0d54bd47.en: Recommends investing in only 4 active skills up to level 20 while emphasizing passive development. "Flame Incineration" gets maximum investment (20+) as primary damage dealer, with "Frost Shock," "Elemental Fusion," "Curse," and "Spatial Domination" assigned to macro/mouse buttons.

6b7585d1.en: Passive priority: 1) Spirit Strike, 2) Concentration, 3) Spirit Revival.

b626ab22.en: Both guides agree "Spirit Strike" is the top passive skill priority confirmed across 2 sources.

2c925551.en: "Elemental Fusion" is described by both as a proc/trigger effect activated when spirits use their own skills, functioning as the core damage amplifier of the rotation, alongside a similarly-described "Space/Spatial Domination" skill.

17da86b9.en: A third guide (fori88.co.kr) gives Korean names that partially resolve two of the naming conflicts above. It confirms 냉기충격 (literally "cold-air shock"), the left-click basic attack that increases attack power on hit and is used to fill cooldown windows kr-era single source ⟦1⟧.

c8d1b7af.en: It also confirms 화염전소 (literally "flame complete-burn"), the right-click basic attack that provides a skill-speed increase and is alternated with the cold skill via a "left-right cancel" during filler time.

4ee0ef56.en: Based on the literal Korean, "Cold Shock" is the more literal rendering of 냉기충격 and "Flame Incineration" (rather than "Flame Transfer") is the more literal rendering of 화염전소, since 전소 means "burned up completely" and gives no basis for a "transfer" translation.

1482473f.en: Translation conflict, partially resolved: the confirmed KR names above show "Cold Shock" and "Flame Incineration" are the more literal English renderings of the two basic-attack skills, and "Flame Transfer" looks like a less literal translation of 화염전소 rather than a separate skill. "Space Domination" vs "Spatial Domination," and "Corrosion" vs "Curse" (used as a Stigma name by one guide, a skill by the other), most likely still reflect different fan translations of the same Korean text rather than different skills.

ae1202a2.en: still contested Whether "Cold Shock" and "Frost Shock" name the same skill remains unresolved: a separate English-language search summary describes "Cold Shock" as a distinct signature skill providing the class's only lifesteal, and "Frost Shock" as a different secondary skill assigned to left and right click for maintaining debuffs, implying they are two separate skills rather than one skill under two fan names single source, exact URL not isolated, from a WebSearch synthesis over multiple Vortex Gaming Spiritmaster guides. No official global name has been found for either skill ⟦1⟧. Net: treat "Cold Shock" (via 냉기충격) as confirmed as a basic-attack skill; treat whether "Frost Shock" refers to the same skill or a different one as unresolved.

a3d186c7.en: No reliable source found for an explicit "avoid these skills" list. Guide A's advice to skip Wind Spirit in the core 3-spirit rotation is the closest equivalent, but this is a PvE efficiency choice, not a "bad skill." Other sources recommend Wind Spirit specifically for escape/chase/disruption utility, so it is situational rather than universally skippable search-summary only, source 403'd ⟦1⟧.

c35633f5.en: Max Flame Incineration, Elemental Fusion, and Cooperative Curse first, with Chill Shock close behind; keep spirit summons and dead skills low.

208d6491.en: This order comes from Korean class boards (Inven, DCinside) and the fori88.co.kr guide blog, all tracking a skill's own level, breakpoints at 8, 12, 16, and a repeated 20 cap, not character level. Treat the levels below as inferred from the shared Stigma and Daevanion unlock schedule, not stated directly by these guides.

f57b53c1.en: primary finisher, needs all four elements active

e7bc423a.en: third must-max damage and debuff skill

bcda6248.en: lifesteal plus attack buff, sustains the rotation

d6c2bdc6.en: secondary combo-link and fear debuff, below the core four

d3853a14.en: share the Skill Point pool with actives, ranked lower

ba8ee543.en: Shock Release (충격 해제) and Spirit Sacrifice (정령 희생): leave at skill level 1, every source that mentions them calls them low value ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

ea0e8aba.en: The four spirit-summon Masteries draw from the same Skill Point pool as the actives above, so stop at skill level 12-16 instead of pushing to 20 ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

603d0a4b.en: 소환: 불의 정령 (Fire), 소환: 물의 정령 (Water), 소환: 땅의 정령 (Earth), 소환: 바람의 정령 (Wind)

456acdf7.en: First: Spirit Strike (정령 타격), named the top passive priority across every source that lists passives ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

67f72d42.en: Then: Mental Concentration (정신 집중), raises direct damage and abnormal-status hit rate ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

d4374275.en: Later: Spirit Regeneration / Spirit Communion (정령 회생 / 정령 교감), resource recovery and survival ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

e2d627e5.en: Push Flame Incineration, Elemental Fusion, and Cooperative Curse; spirit priority is contested from the start

f8b659b1.en: Follow the skill point order above for actives.

fb810632.en: fori88.co.kr calls Wind Spirit the mandatory first summon for Cooperative Curse synergy ⟦1⟧

c33dc875.en: A separate Inven thread instead ranks Wind Spirit as the single highest-priority summon, kept permanently active on its own hotbar ⟦1⟧

848c6b8f.en: This conflicts with the 3-spirit Fire/Water/Earth rotation in the Rotation and combos card below, which excludes Wind Spirit ⟦1⟧

5c6c2017.en: Daevanion board opens: raise skill-level nodes before stat nodes

d5425c3e.en: A KR source puts Mastery skill-level nodes before stat nodes, then orange end-branch nodes ⟦1⟧

2c052c52.en: Stigma opens: slot Grace of Spirit and Ancient Spirit first

297e980a.en: Level 정령의 가호/가오 (Grace of Spirit) then 고대의 정령 (Ancient Spirit) to skill level 20, the two top picks per a dedicated Inven thread ⟦1⟧

a424d60d.en: Next, 불길의 축복 (Blessing of Flame) to skill level 20 for party synergy ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

e2c2047a.en: 협공: 부식 (Cooperative Corrosion) to skill level 20 rounds out the core four, a DoT plus roughly 10% all-resistance reduction ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

59a4ce0f.en: Keep feeding Skill Points into the core four actives before the spirit Masteries

86c0849a.en: This stretch continues the same skill-level order until points allow the spirit Masteries their turn ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

1ef15419.en: What changes: only skill-level breakpoints matter now

5bbf87b9.en: Sources tie the power spike to spirit-cycle mastery, not a level number; see Skill priority above, and the Stigma picks and Daevanion board route cards below, ⟦1⟧

28f3d81e.en: Level Water Spirit and Fire Spirit to at least skill level 16 as a practical floor before investing further ⟦1⟧

054472e9.en: Spirit priority is contested: fori88.co.kr calls Wind Spirit the mandatory first summon for Cooperative Curse synergy, and a separate Inven thread ranks it as the single highest-priority summon kept permanently active ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧. The 3-spirit Fire/Water/Earth rotation in the Rotation and combos card below excludes Wind Spirit instead ⟦3⟧.

4de1c231.en: Avoid: maxing the four spirit-summon Masteries past skill level 16. They share the same Skill Point pool as the four core actives, and Korean guides say directly not to push them to 20, invest to 16 or just 12 instead ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

a7382488.en: Stigmas unlock at 23 with 5 slots; PvE favors pet output and DoT uptime, PvP favors debilitation effects.

ee28e67b.en: Stigmas unlock at level 23 with up to 5 slots after the March 25, 2026 KR patch (shared system fact) kr-era, balance may change ⟦1⟧.

fbcea17e.en: That same patch added a new Spiritmaster-specific Stigma called "Command: Proxy," which reworks an existing skill named "Kaisinel's Power" into a party buff granting +20% status accuracy/resistance, alongside several spirit skills being converted into AoE effects ⟦1⟧.

b048326b.en: Level "Corrosion" and "Fixed Spirit" to rank 5 first

71144bdb.en: Remaining slots from "Shadow of Curse," "Flame Blessing," or additional "Corrosion" depending on preference single source, unconfirmed wording

92244dab.en: Vortex Gaming's guide independently lists Stigma priorities as "Blessing of Fire" (accuracy/crit/damage amplification), "Protection" (defensive spirit ability), "Stabilization" (consistency), "Corrosion" (debuff damage), and "Blood Drain" (an HP-based shield, called a strong defensive pick for hard content) ⟦1⟧.

0084d8dc.en: Translation conflict: "Corrosion" and "Blessing of Fire"/"Flame Blessing" appear across both guidance sets above, giving moderate (2-source) confidence to those two specifically, though naming again varies slightly between sources.

935c4509.en: PvE vs PvP: aion2boost.com frames PvE Stigma priority as pet output and DoT uptime first, control second; PvP priority as debilitation effects (fear/drain) first, then pet resilience/pressure, then survivability for extended trades ⟦1⟧.

a7823a08.en: Summarized by that source as "pet-facing investment outvalues caster-facing investment at equal cost."

4f276f9f.en: No reliable source found for a confirmed advanced Stigma (level 45) list for Spiritmaster specifically, or for a definitive "spend Stigma Shards on X first" recommendation beyond the general cross-class advice to fund frequently-used Stigmas before spreading investment ⟦1⟧.

723b932b.en: Shared board system; raise main skill levels and take orange end-branch nodes before minor skill levels.

6a1c0fc1.en: Shared system mechanics (see the Sorcerer guide for the full node-color and board-unlock breakdown): board unlocks at level 12 (Nezekan), with further boards at 20 (Zikel), 30 (Vaizel), 40 (Triniel), and advanced boards at 45 (Ariel for PvE, Azphel for PvP, plus Marchutan and Yustiel referenced in one source) ⟦1⟧.

b8b6e956.en: Node types: grey = stats (1 point), green = passives (2 points), blue = active skills (3 points), orange = unique board-specialty bonuses (4 points), same source.

21d75ce8.en: For Spiritmaster specifically, aion2boost.com's PvE priority order (pet output and resilience first, DoT uptime second, control third) implies favoring Daevanion nodes that raise spirit-related active skills and their survivability stats before general caster stat nodes marketing source, inferential ⟦1⟧.

d980518f.en: A KR skill-tree and combo guide gives an explicit Spiritmaster Daevanion priority order:

62e89604.en: Raise skill levels on main abilities toward specific targets, levels 16 and 12 are commonly cited breakpoints, before taking orange end-branch nodes

b1944358.en: Take orange end-branch nodes for damage amplification, cooldown reduction, combat speed, and crit-damage resistance

366cc89a.en: Take minor skill levels and multi-hit-related nodes last

d5216f75.en: This order is single-source and general within the class rather than tied to specific named nodes on the board, but it is the most concrete Spiritmaster-specific Daevanion guidance found so far. It broadly agrees with the general cross-class "prioritize active/blue nodes early" advice.

3e94a44c.en: Essential Spiritmaster Arcana picks are Spirit's Majesty, Corrosion, and Inferno; treat exact names as provisional.

6e1a7740.en: Arcana is a shared cross-class system (see the Sorcerer guide for slot types, grades, and Training Arcana values) kr-era, balance may change ⟦1⟧.

f693d412.en: The general DPS-class advice, prioritize cards raising levels on the active skills and passives driving your main rotation, then complete damage-oriented sets, applies to Spiritmaster as a DPS class, but the source gives no Spiritmaster-specific card names or slot priorities.

07ce942b.en: Essential: Spirit's Majesty (survival and buff core), Corrosion (DoT and debuff application), Inferno (flame damage output)

076275a9.en: Optional but recommended: Absorption (30 second cooldown, HP recovery, stable play), Onslaught of Ruin (60 second cooldown, high DPS plus a groggy value of 50, described as less convenient to use)

51bbad19.en: These are fan-translated names from a single KR guide, not confirmed official terms kr-era single source, fan-translated names ⟦1⟧.

0a161238.en: This card list is single-source and KR-era. Treat exact card names as provisional until a second source or global localization confirms them; no Spiritmaster-specific card slotting order beyond "essential vs optional" was found, and no source names cards to avoid.

6a928265.en: Orb is the only weapon; Magic Attack, Spirit Efficiency, HP/Defense, Mana Regen, and Accuracy form the stat foundation.

f86e6404.en: Weapon: Orb (confirmed across all sources). Stat priority, per a PvP-build-focused guide: Magic Attack, Spirit Efficiency, HP/Defense, Mana Regeneration, and Accuracy "form the foundation" ⟦1⟧.

7a9b69e2.en: Do first: a high-magic-attack Orb with spell power, general advice for DPS classes is to upgrade the weapon first

a15d5d5e.en: Then: HP for survivability, since the caster is a sustained-pressure class

82bb25ec.en: Later / optional: Mana Regeneration and Accuracy to round out the "foundation" stats

b78fd407.en: Detailed gear stat breakpoints from Vortex Gaming's PvE build (single source, KR-era, terminology likely translation-specific): pursue "Perfect" quality options on pants, cloaks, shoes, and gloves single source, numeric values unverifiable ⟦1⟧.

d9ae1cc9.en: Prioritize Attack Power (cited around 258) and Critical Hit/Accuracy (cited around 147) on stat rolls.

b28c60dc.en: For Awakening (an enhancement tier) prioritize Damage Resistance, Amplification, Critical Damage, and Impact; for "magic stones" (the manastone/godstone-equivalent socket system), "Weapon Damage Increase" is called the most efficient choice.

72526cfb.en: For PvP, the same source recommends Awakening priorities of HP, Status Effect Resistance, Iron Wall, Impact Resistance, and Damage Resistance, plus a "PVP Damage Amplification" magic stone (Advanced Abyss variant) or "Vitality" as an efficient alternative.

ef8e3fc3.en: Describes Spiritmaster in PvP as "a straightforward damage-trading class with no CC, movement skills, or slows."

79796d20.en: Document fear/root/knockback tools: Soul's Cry, Ashy Call, Earth Spirit bind, Wind Spirit knockback/silence.

060dab8a.en: Contested: the "no CC, movement skills, or slows" claim is in clear tension with the fear/root/knockback kit documented by two other sources above. This looks like an error or an oversimplification in the vortexgaming.io PvP section rather than a genuine build difference.

9d58df7b.en: Manastone/Godstone-equivalent system (shared, general description in the Sorcerer guide): sockets on gear, Manastones for weapon/armor, Spiritstones for accessories, Godstones for extra combat effects, resettable via soul imprinting kr-era ⟦1⟧.

22884a02.en: No reliable source found for confirmed Spiritmaster set-effect names.

ffe60e82.en: Keep a spirit alive and buffed before you summon it; damage collapses the moment a spirit expires.

0e4baddd.en: Core mechanic, confirmed across multiple sources: keeping spirits alive and actively rotated is "the single biggest factor in Spiritmaster output," with damage falling off sharply once summons expire ⟦1⟧.

009a2cad.en: The "Warala" rotation concept (single source, KR-derived term, spelling and translation not independently confirmed): rather than keeping one persistent spirit summoned, the class repeatedly re-summons spirits to retrigger on-summon effects (named "Space/Spatial Domination" and "Elemental Fusion") frequently ⟦1⟧.

039c03bb.en: A 3-spirit rotation (Fire, Water, Earth) is recommended over a 4-spirit rotation, since adding Wind Spirit is said to slow the cycle and reduce overall damage efficiency.

f146e474.en: Vortex Gaming, single source, KR-era: keep the skill macro limited to one skill ("Flame Incineration"), and manually trigger "Frost Shock," "Elemental Fusion," "Curse," and "Spatial Domination" via separate mouse buttons, pressing them continuously to maintain debuff uptime.

14d635c0.en: At higher gear/skill levels, replace some summons with basic attacks; keep Water Spirit and re-summon it roughly every 15 seconds for its single-target damage

397ed56d.en: Buff-before-summon timing rule (a specifically called-out beginner mistake): activate buffs such as "Blessing of Fire" and "Protection" before summoning "Ancient Spirit," because spirits inherit the caster's current stat bonuses at the moment they are summoned. Buffing after summoning wastes the effect for that spirit's lifetime ⟦1⟧.

0432dc3e.en: Fire Spirit: offensive summon, applies a Burning DoT and reduces enemy Defense (one detailed source cites 150 damage/sec and a 30% Defense reduction, single-source numeric figure) ⟦1⟧

cee25a1e.en: Water Spirit: healing, cleansing, and shields (same source cites 370 HP per 3 seconds, single-source figure), described elsewhere as the class's primary sustain tool during long fights ⟦1⟧

370c03eb.en: Earth Spirit: gives a damage-reduction shield and can Knock Down/Bind enemies, called "one of the most complete tank pets"

a66c0963.en: Wind Spirit: knocks back and silences, boosts the caster's own movement speed, functioning as the class's escape/chase/disruption tool ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

59af23a8.en: Combo/utility skill: "Command: Substitution" causes the active spirit to absorb 100% of the caster's incoming damage within a 15-meter radius for 30 seconds, described as a major defensive cooldown that can be paired with a "Spirit Sacrifice" effect for large defensive or offensive payoff ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

d1189596.en: Situational spirit pairings recommended by one source (single source, contested against the "3-spirit Warala" advice above, which specifically favors Fire/Water/Earth): PvE sustain = Earth + Water; PvP control = Fire + Wind; solo farming efficiency = Fire + Earth contested ⟦1⟧.

7be3a0a6.en: No reliable, verified source found for a documented dedicated "auto-hunt" skill setup separate from the manual macro descriptions above.

95052c1e.en: One of the strongest solo classes: the spirit tanks for you, and it wins fights through attrition, not burst.

bd8047a0.en: Solo leveling comfort is rated as strong: Spiritmaster is repeatedly described as "one of the strongest solo classes," with the spirit acting as a built-in frontline/tank so the caster is not the sole damage sponge ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ (describing "solo safety via personal frontline").

e9f14340.en: Sustain is comparatively good thanks to Water Spirit's healing/cleanse and Siphon's lifesteal, though damage output is explicitly tied to keeping a spirit alive and correctly positioned, so sustain and damage both collapse together if spirit uptime lapses ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧.

5173da02.en: No reliable source found with Spiritmaster-specific pull-size guidance. General framing from aion2boost.com is that the class wins fights through attrition rather than burst, so players should "embrace attrition pacing" rather than expect quick single-cast kills ⟦1⟧.

406a3684.en: When the class "turns on": sources agree the class becomes meaningfully stronger once the player has internalized spirit-cycle management, summon timing, buff-before-summon sequencing, and Elemental Fusion triggers, rather than at a specific level breakpoint. No reliable source ties this to an exact level number.

1b585b6d.en: Most mistakes come from letting a spirit die, buffing too late, or under-investing in pet-facing nodes.

d10f120b.en: Treating Spiritmaster as a "simple pet class" and being overwhelmed once the actual rotation depth (spirit cycling, not button-mashing) becomes apparent ⟦1⟧

803cfb7c.en: Letting spirits die before re-summoning instead of summoning preemptively to maintain continuous uptime ⟦1⟧

8cdbc128.en: Buffing after summoning "Ancient Spirit" instead of before, since the spirit inherits the caster's buffs only at the moment of summoning ⟦1⟧

62ab51aa.en: Wasting spirits by summoning them outside the effective combat area, or summoning right before a forced reset/phase change ⟦1⟧

bd98edce.en: Adding a fourth spirit (Wind) to the core PvE rotation when a tighter 3-spirit cycle is reportedly more damage-efficient contested, Wind is also recommended for PvP/escape ⟦1⟧

ee7b46a2.en: Ignoring positioning relative to your own spirit, losing access to spirit-granted shields/heals that require proximity ⟦1⟧

7abdb2d7.en: Spamming fear/CC on cooldown instead of using it to lock a specific threat at the right moment, "fear locks opponents strategically, not spam" ⟦1⟧

96c718c9.en: Assuming pet damage alone carries fights in high-end PvE without accounting for boss movement disrupting spirit positioning, which several sources flag as the class's biggest competitive-PvE weakness ⟦1⟧

f5a7e63a.en: Underinvesting in pet-facing Stigma/Daevanion nodes in favor of caster-facing ones, when the framing is that "pet-facing investment outvalues caster-facing investment at equal cost" ⟦1⟧

2f637e2e.en: Version note: AION 2 has been live in KR/TW since November 2025. Global PC launch is October 5, 2026, with a fully wiped Launch Scale Test on September 17-18 that does not carry over. Most Cleric guides below are KR/TW-era. A reported August 2026 balance patch cut fixed healing passives in favor of attack-power-scaling healing, reportedly pushing Cleric toward C-tier single source ⟦1⟧. Treat any older "S-tier healer" claim as stale.

f8f8ef67.en: Cleric wields a Mace paired with a shield or magic offhand ("Guard") for a tankier build, with a Staff option for higher magic boost and more damage ⟦1⟧.

0abfd231.en: AION2 Hub describes it as a back-line healer who cycles AoE and over-time heals plus protective shields to sustain the group ⟦1⟧.

69cf599e.en: Only class that can actively dispel debuffs, and carries the signature Summon Resurrection skill, making it near-mandatory for dungeon groups confirmed, multiple sources ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

d95b51c7.en: Fextralife calls it "an indispensable character in party play," but says it specializes in AoE healing over single-target: "the Cleric's healing alone will not be enough" if the party ignores mechanics ⟦1⟧

8a3e5f38.en: Party demand: very high, near-mandatory for dungeons and raids

70b42630.en: PvE: strong utility pick from its heal, shield, cleanse and res kit, though the August 2026 patch reportedly weakened fixed healing passives marketing source ⟦1⟧

890ef8ad.en: PvP: viable as a "survival healer" build, but reportedly slipped to C-tier alongside Chanter after the same patch single source ⟦1⟧

03fd32d9.en: Solo: good. Fextralife calls it "accessible for solo players"; other guides call it tanky and safe to solo, kill speed aside, thanks to self-sustain from its own healing kit ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧

5012a282.en: Beginner tip: pick Cleric if you want a forgiving, hard-to-kill class with guaranteed group invites and don't mind managing cooldown rhythm and positioning over raw damage numbers.

5f7da174.en: Keep a heal and a damage skill both leveled; the exact global-launch order is unconfirmed, so treat lists below as directional.

70a9d668.en: Gap: no reliable source found for a precise, level-by-level global-launch skill point order. The lists below are pieced together from KR/TW-era guides and should be treated as directional, not exact.

e68fb845.en: Do first: keep 1-2 healing skills (Healing Light / Light of Regeneration) leveled alongside your main damage chain.

02f8b1c4.en: A Cleric with no heal rank is unplayable in groups, and one with no damage rank kills too slowly solo (synthesized from the sources below).

3e4195cb.en: Do first: below level 20, spec Divine Retribution 2 and 4 to leverage the spirit synergy ⟦1⟧

982bfd16.en: Then (PvE, level 20+): Divine Retribution (2/3/4), Judgment Bolt (2/4/5), Sacred Energy (3/4/5), Light of Regeneration (1/4/5), Troops (2/3/4) ⟦1⟧

ede203b0.en: Sacred Energy is a higher DPS priority; Troops hits max DPS with a full charge.

c4c3bb8e.en: Then (PvP): shift Light of Regeneration to 1/2/5 (defense over mobility), Troops to 3/4 (full-charge windows are rarer in PvP), and Shock Release to 1/4 or 1/5 at level 16+ ⟦1⟧

93e0206b.en: Later / optional: a separate arcana-tied guide orders leveling as Forge first (highest DPS), then Swift Heal, Earth's Retribution, Rain of Healing, Troops, and Lightning Judgment ⟦1⟧

deceb2f3.en: That guide suggests reducing Light of Regeneration below level 16 to free points.

7ad96335.en: Divine Retribution, Judgment Bolt, Sacred Energy, Light of Regeneration, Troops as the level 20+ PvE core ⟦1⟧

48f91902.en: Forge, Swift Heal, Earth's Retribution, Rain of Healing, Troops, Lightning Judgment, with Light of Regeneration deprioritized early ⟦1⟧

bdf0d2a9.en: These two guides partially conflict on Light of Regeneration's priority; treat as contested, not confirmed.

ba7f4453.en: Playstyle: weaving damage skills between healing cycles to maintain mana efficiency. A basic solo leveling loop cited elsewhere is applying Punishment Seal, spamming Holy Strike, and healing as needed marketing, lower trust.

71429e93.en: Push Earth's Retribution and Heavenly Judgment first, keep Divine Grace and Earth's Blessing maxed, then take Divine Burst as your first Stigma.

a6878adf.en: This order comes from the one Inven post that frames leveling by skill-level band, cross-checked against an aggregated early-priority search summary ⟦1⟧.

16f69343.en: Every "Lv" figure below is the skill's own level (its 8/12/16/20 spec breakpoints), not your character level, confirmed by a DCInside thread discussing a Stigma at "level 15" while still leveling ⟦1⟧.

f2580478.en: 면죄 (Absolution) follows at Stigma Lv 5, then 10, for cleanse plus heal utility; a DCInside thread shows a player choosing between Absolution and Salvation at Stigma Lv 15, so both are viable early picks ⟦1⟧

fcc9862d.en: Beginner tip: spend Stigma Shards first on stigmas already equipped in your main rotation before funding alternates, and pick ones that unlock a specialization effect at a reachable level over spreading thin ⟦1⟧.

d59ff75d.en: Build one full rotation on Mastery skills first, then fund the Daevanion nodes that support it; no Cleric-specific route is confirmed.

be7fd0d4.en: The Daevanion board is a node-investment system spent with Daevanion Points, gated by character level. This is a general system note, not Cleric-specific ⟦1⟧.

df8c26bf.en: Node cost tiers (general system): Grey (stat) 1 point, Green (passive skill) 2 points, Blue (active skill) 3 points, Orange (unique skill) 4 points single source aggregation

c756378f.en: For a healer specifically: prioritize your main damage chain skill and any node that boosts an HP-recovery skill or a skill usable while moving

da0043ae.en: General guidance: build one full rotation on Mastery skills first, fund the Stigmas used in that rotation, trace the cheapest Daevanion path that supports the same build, and only reset when your role changes meaningfully.

d4f671d3.en: Daevanion Points and Crystals come from leveling/quests, achievements, and content activities ⟦1⟧.

76313528.en: Chalice: aim for 2+ of these skills on one card - Forge, Swift Heal, Earth's Retribution, Rain of Healing, Troops, Lightning Judgment ⟦1⟧

059f225c.en: Bell: priority order is Divine Grace (minimum level 3), then Shield of Immortality, then Warm Aura

986b60d4.en: Scales: get at least 2 useful active skills on the card since it "heavily influences your overall setup direction"

815ffc5e.en: Version note: AION 2 has been live in KR/TW since November 2025. Global PC launch is October 5, 2026, with a fully wiped Launch Scale Test on September 17-18. Nearly all Chanter guides below are KR/TW-era. A reported August 2026 balance patch removed fixed healing passives in favor of attack-power-scaling healing, which one source says dropped Chanter to C-tier alongside Cleric single source ⟦1⟧.

6221ffe8.en: Possibly Aion 1: some search results for this class returned original-Aion fan wiki pages (aion.fandom.com, differ.blog, an aspirine.su stigma calculator) rather than AION 2 sources. Those are excluded from claims below except where explicitly flagged as a conflation risk.

112cbb3f.en: Chanter is a hybrid support/melee class. AION2 Hub calls it a "Staff-wielding hybrid priest who buffs, heals, and fights on the front line" ⟦1⟧.

aa15beeb.en: Fextralife similarly describes it as a hybrid support that increases ally stats during party play and can function in several roles simultaneously, from buffer to a secondary healer or damage dealer ⟦1⟧.

166d5e88.en: Weapon: Staff. Unlike the original AION, Chanter can now block effectively with the staff itself, removing the old mace-and-shield swap so Staff is the single weapon for offense and defense single source.

e13154fb.en: AION2 Hub frames it precisely: Chanter is "never the main healer, yet able to keep a group standing while contributing real damage," trading peak healing output for survivability and offense, a "sustain-and-support bruiser" ⟦1⟧.

e019e7e4.en: Fextralife notes a mechanical limitation: the class lacks instant single-target heals but excels with AoE regeneration zones, and cites beta feedback calling it "a hybrid healer with high DPS and strong self-sustain" ⟦1⟧.

475a5d90.en: Difficulty and grade: one build-guide site rates Chanter Medium difficulty, PvE grade B, PvP grade B single source ⟦1⟧

2440cf5b.en: Caveat: "its grade is a function of your roster, not just your hands," over-performing in premades and merely hitting its stated B tier in solo queue.

4077d44f.en: Party demand: called "the clear top choice if your priority is party buffs." single source aggregation

a12c435b.en: Runs a Mantra-based toolkit with offensive, defensive, and utility benefits.

07c965b1.en: The build most players will expect for group content like dungeons, rift battles, world bosses, and guild raids. This contrasts with Cleric's more universal, role-agnostic demand.

52e69630.en: Solo viability is contested between sources.

b4cabb15.en: aion2boost.com is more skeptical: solo viability is "modest as a standalone bruiser" because the class struggles without allies to benefit from its buffs, making solo play less rewarding than group content ⟦1⟧

496e5c3a.en: Net read: Chanter solos fine numerically, but its unique value is wasted when alone.
